# MM-P1-L4-CN01 - Maintenance manual - Heat Treat CNC turning center #1

Revision: Rev E  
Plant: P1, line P1-L4  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L4-CN01

Scope
- Routine mechanical and operational maintenance for EQ-P1-L4-CN01 in P1-L4 heat treat cell.
- Tasks cover chuck jaw bolt verification, spindle warm-up procedure, and visual inspections required before production handoff.
- Refer to MM-P1-L4-CN01-S2, SB-1046, SOP-P1-L4-01 for related procedures and safety bulletins.

Tools
- Torque wrench calibrated for specified chuck jaw bolt torque.
- Manufacturer-approved cleaning brushes and lint-free wipes.
- Personal protective equipment per SOP-P1-L4-01.
- Routine inspection lamp and mirror.

Procedure
- Verify machine is in a stopped and locked state following SOP-P1-L4-01 before any mechanical work.
- Inspect chuck, jaws, and mounting surfaces for foreign material; remove debris with lint-free wipes.
- For chuck jaw bolt verification: set torque wrench to 90 N·m and sequentially verify each chuck jaw bolt reaches specified torque. Do not exceed or under-torque bolts.
- Close chuck and cycle manually to confirm smooth travel and repeatability; correct any binding per MM-P1-L4-CN01-S2.
- Perform spindle warm-up following the warm-up schedule in the controller: run warm-up cycle until spindle has completed the programmed ramp. Ensure cumulative spindle warm-up time equals 15 minutes before loading production parts.
- After warm-up, perform a light test cut on a sacrificial workpiece per SB-1046 to confirm surface finish and concentricity.
- Record all findings, torque readings, and any corrective actions in the maintenance log and notify line supervision if out-of-tolerance conditions are found.

Acceptance criteria
- All chuck jaw bolts verified at 90 N·m.
- Spindle has completed a 15 minutes warm-up and controller indicates ready state per SOP-P1-L4-01.
- Test cut meets dimensional and surface criteria referenced in SB-1046.
- Maintenance log completed and cross-referenced to MM-P1-L4-CN01-S2.
title: Maintenance manual - Heat Treat CNC turning center #1

text:
# MM-P1-L4-HP02 - Maintenance manual - Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #2
Revision: Rev B  
Plant: P1, line P1-L4  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L4-HP02

## Scope
This document defines preventive and corrective maintenance tasks for the Heat Treat hydraulic forging press EQ-P1-L4-HP02. It covers mechanical fastening verification, hydraulic system pressure limit verification, and functional checks necessary to return the press to service after maintenance. For operating procedures and lockout-tagout, see SOP-P1-L4-01, SOP-P1-L4-02, and SOP-P1-L4-03.

## Tools
- Torque wrench capable of reaching the main ram bolt torque specified below.
- Hydraulic pressure gauge compatible with machine test ports.
- Standard hand tools and safety equipment per site PPE policy.

## Procedure
- Verify area is secured and procedures in SOP-P1-L4-01 and SOP-P1-L4-02 are followed prior to entry.
- Isolate hydraulic power and relieve residual pressure following SOP-P1-L4-03.
- Inspect the main ram and surrounding bolted joints for visible damage or displacement.
- Using the torque wrench, set and apply the main ram bolt torque for EQ-P1-L4-HP02 to 970 N·m. Confirm each relevant fastener reaches the specified torque and document readings.
- Install the hydraulic pressure gauge at the designated test port. Restore hydraulic power and monitor system pressure while operating controls at minimal demand. Verify the system pressure limit for EQ-P1-L4-HP02 does not exceed 300 bar during test cycles.
- If pressure approaches or exceeds the specified limit, stop operation immediately, isolate the system, and execute troubleshooting per SOP-P1-L4-02 and SOP-P1-L4-03.
- After tests, remove test equipment, restore system to standard configuration, and complete maintenance record entries.

## Acceptance criteria
- All main ram bolts torqued to 970 N·m and recorded in the maintenance log.
- Operational pressure validated and confirmed not to exceed 300 bar under test conditions.
- No abnormal leaks, noises, or visible deformations observed during functional test.
- Work order closed with references to SOP-P1-L4-01, SOP-P1-L4-02, and SOP-P1-L4-03 and signature of the technician and supervisor.
title: Maintenance manual - Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #2

text:
# MM-P1-L4-HT03 - Maintenance manual - Heat Treat heat treat furnace #3

Revision: Rev C  
Plant: P1, line P1-L4  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L4-HT03  
Related documents: ECN-2026-002, SB-1006, SOP-P1-L4-02

Scope
This document defines required maintenance actions for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P1-L4-HT03). It covers preventive maintenance tasks, required tools, detailed procedure for routine checks, and acceptance criteria to confirm safe and repeatable operation. Refer to ECN-2026-002, SB-1006, and SOP-P1-L4-02 for design changes and operating procedures.

Tools
- Portable calibrated thermometer (as required by SOP-P1-L4-02)  
- Hand tools and insulated gloves per site PPE requirements (see SB-1006)  
- Calibration standard and documentation forms referenced in ECN-2026-002

Procedure
- Verify work area is safe and furnace is in standby following SOP-P1-L4-02.  
- Inspect chamber lining, door seals, and visible heating elements for integrity; address any damage per ECN-2026-002.  
- Verify control system connectivity and examine indicators for error codes; escalate per SB-1006 if present.  
- The austenitizing setpoint for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P1-L4-HT03) is 880 °C. Confirm setpoint matches control display.  
- Perform thermocouple check and document offset per calibration standard. The thermocouple calibration interval for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P1-L4-HT03) is 95 days. Schedule next calibration in accordance with that interval and record in maintenance log.  
- Perform functional run to confirm stable ramp and soak behavior as described in SOP-P1-L4-02. Record observations and any deviations.

Acceptance criteria
- Control setpoint matches documented value: The austenitizing setpoint for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P1-L4-HT03) is 880 °C.  
- Thermocouple calibration current and recorded next calibration meet site schedule: The thermocouple calibration interval for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P1-L4-HT03) is 95 days.  
- No active alarms or unresolved errors per SB-1006.

# MM-P2-L1-RR01 - Maintenance manual - Hot Forge radial ring rolling mill #1

Revision: Rev A  
Plant: P2, line P2-L1  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L1-RR01

Scope
This document covers preventive maintenance for Hot Forge radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P2-L1-RR01) limited to mechanical clamp and main roll bearing lubrication tasks. It supplements SOP-P2-L1-01 and SOP-P2-L1-02 and implements changes from ECN-2026-023 where applicable.

Tools
- Torque wrench calibrated for mandrel clamp bolt torque.  
- Grease gun compatible with the bearing grease specified in SOP-P2-L1-01.  
- Inspection mirror, lint-free cloth, and appropriate personal protective equipment per SOP-P2-L1-02.

Procedure
Inspect mandrel clamp assembly for wear and secure fit. Clean mating surfaces and remove debris using lint-free cloth. Apply thread treatment per SOP-P2-L1-01 if required. Tighten mandrel clamp bolt to the mandrel clamp bolt torque for Hot Forge radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P2-L1-RR01) is 430 N·m. Verify bolt seating and clamp alignment after torque application.

Lubricate main roll bearings following the lubrication channel access procedures in SOP-P2-L1-01. The main roll bearing lubrication interval for Hot Forge radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P2-L1-RR01) is 220 hours. Purge old grease from the bearing housing until new grease is visible at the relief point, then apply the quantity and type specified in SOP-P2-L1-01. Record lubrication events in the equipment log and reference ECN-2026-023 for any material or procedural updates.

Acceptance criteria
Mandrel clamp bolt maintains specified torque and clamp shows no movement under operational verification. Bearing housings accept grease and show consistent grease return at relief points. No metal particles or contamination present in grease after purge. All actions documented in the equipment log and cross-referenced to SOP-P2-L1-01, SOP-P2-L1-02, and ECN-2026-023.
title: Maintenance manual - Hot Forge radial ring rolling mill #1

# MM-P2-L1-IH02 - Maintenance manual - Hot Forge induction billet heater #2

Revision: Rev C  
Plant: P2, line P2-L1  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L1-IH02

Scope
- This document covers routine preventive maintenance tasks required to verify operation and safety of Hot Forge induction billet heater #2 (EQ-P2-L1-IH02). Tasks address mechanical inspection, electrical integrity checks, cooling system verification, and temperature validation to maintain process readiness.

Tools
- Insulated hand tools compatible with induction systems
- Thermal imaging camera or calibrated pyrometer
- Flow meter capable of reading coil cooling water flow
- Lockout/tagout kit and PPE per site requirements

Procedure
- Perform lockout/tagout on EQ-P2-L1-IH02 per SOP-P2-L1-01 before any work on the unit.
- Visually inspect coil assembly and high-current connections for damage, discoloration, or loose fittings. Tighten fittings as required using proper insulated tools.
- Inspect cooling lines, hoses, and fittings for signs of leaks or wear. Replace components that show degradation.
- Verify coil cooling water flow through the coil circuit using the flow meter. Confirm coil cooling water flow minimum for Hot Forge induction billet heater #2 (EQ-P2-L1-IH02) is 55 L/min.
- Energize the unit per SOP-P2-L1-01 and bring a representative billet up to the target process temperature. Confirm the target billet temperature for Hot Forge induction billet heater #2 (EQ-P2-L1-IH02) is 1180 °C using a calibrated thermal device.
- Record observed temperatures, flow rates, and any anomalies. If deviations are observed, tag the unit out of service and initiate corrective action referencing ECN-2026-013 and ECN-2026-039.

Acceptance criteria
- No visible damage or loose high-current connections after inspection.
- Cooling system shows no leaks and meets coil cooling water flow minimum for Hot Forge induction billet heater #2 (EQ-P2-L1-IH02) of 55 L/min.
- Billet temperature reaches the target billet temperature for Hot Forge induction billet heater #2 (EQ-P2-L1-IH02) of 1180 °C under normal operating conditions.
- All actions and measurements documented and filed according to SOP-P2-L1-01 and referenced ECN documents: ECN-2026-013, ECN-2026-039.
title: Maintenance manual - Hot Forge induction billet heater #2

# MM-P2-L1-SB03 Maintenance manual - Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #3

Revision: Rev A  
Plant: P2, line P2-L1  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L1-SB03

Scope
This document defines routine maintenance for Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P2-L1-SB03) to ensure blast performance, operator safety, and component life. Use this procedure in conjunction with ECN-2026-033, ECN-2026-036, and SOP-P2-L1-01.

Tools
- Impact driver, hand tools set, inspection mirror, flashlight, magnetic tray.
- Torque wrench capable of reading 50 N·m for verification.
- Shop vacuum and replacement filter cartridge appropriate for cabinet dust outlet.

Procedure
- Isolate electrical supply and lock out per SOP-P2-L1-01 before any access. Verify zero energy state.
- Open access doors and perform visual inspection of liner, wheel, and media containment areas with flashlight and mirror.
- The blast wheel liner bolt torque for Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P2-L1-SB03) is 50 N·m. Check each liner bolt for tightness and apply the specified torque with a calibrated torque wrench.
- Confirm shot delivery system clearances visually and remove build-up using non-sparking tools only.
- The shot media top-up interval for Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P2-L1-SB03) is 33 hours. Record runtime and replenish media to maintain minimum charge as described in ECN-2026-033.
- Inspect dust collector interface and replace filter cartridge if visibly loaded. Use shop vacuum to remove loose dust.
- Reassemble access panels, remove lockout, and perform a short functional run per SOP-P2-L1-01 to confirm normal operation.

Acceptance criteria
- Liner bolts are torqued to 50 N·m and show no signs of loosening after the functional run.
- Shot media level records indicate top-up performed at 33 hours intervals and media flow is consistent.
- No abnormal vibration, noise, or leakage observed during the functional run; cabinet performance meets baseline in ECN-2026-036.
- All actions are documented and signed per SOP-P2-L1-01.
title: Maintenance manual - Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #3

# MM-P2-L2-IH01 - Maintenance manual - Ring Rolling induction billet heater #1

Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P2, line P2-L2  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L2-IH01

Scope
- Routine maintenance and operational verification for Ring Rolling induction billet heater #1 (EQ-P2-L2-IH01). Applies to mechanical, electrical, and cooling systems associated with the unit. Refer to ECN-2026-012 and ECN-2026-048 for design changes and SOP-P2-L2-05 for standard operating procedures.

Tools
- Basic insulated hand tools, multimeter, clamp meter, vibration pickup, thermal camera, and water flow meter calibrated per plant practice. Use PPE as required by SOP-P2-L2-05.

Procedure
- Isolate power and lockout/tagout per SOP-P2-L2-05 before access. Verify LOTO status with multimeter.
- Visually inspect coil assembly and buswork for signs of damage, discoloration, or loose connections. Address findings in accordance with ECN-2026-012.
- Inspect cooling water supply and return lines for leaks, erosion, and proper routing. Clean strainers and verify unobstructed flow path.
- Measure coil cooling water flow with the calibrated flow meter. Confirm coil cooling water flow minimum for Ring Rolling induction billet heater #1 (EQ-P2-L2-IH01) is 81 L/min. Record measured value on the maintenance log and attach to the work order.
- Power-up following SOP-P2-L2-05 and perform a controlled heat sequence. Use thermal camera and process indicators to confirm uniform heating.
- Confirm the target billet temperature for Ring Rolling induction billet heater #1 (EQ-P2-L2-IH01) is 1230 °C during process validation runs. Record temperature verification and any deviations.
- Restore panels, remove LOTO, and return unit to service per SOP-P2-L2-05.

Acceptance criteria
- No active electrical faults or abnormal vibration signatures present after maintenance. 
- Coil cooling water flow meets or exceeds 81 L/min as recorded. 
- Billet heating achieves and sustains 1230 °C during validation checks. 
- All findings documented and corrective actions tracked; design discrepancies referenced to ECN-2026-048.
title: Maintenance manual - Ring Rolling induction billet heater #1

text:
# MM-P2-L2-HT02 - Maintenance manual - Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #2

Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P2, line P2-L2  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L2-HT02

Scope
- This document defines preventive maintenance, thermocouple calibration, and setpoint verification for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L2-HT02). Applies to personnel authorized by plant supervision. Refer to MM-P2-L2-HT02-S1 for supplemental drawings and SOP-P2-L2-02 and SOP-P2-L2-05 for safety and lockout/tagout procedures.

Tools
- Multimeter or thermocouple calibrator compatible with furnace thermocouples.
- Calibration reference standard traceable to plant laboratory.
- Insulated gloves and heat-resistant PPE as required by SOP-P2-L2-02.
- Basic hand tools for access panels per MM-P2-L2-HT02-S1.

Procedure
1. Verify authorization and review SOP-P2-L2-02 and SOP-P2-L2-05 before starting work.
2. Perform lockout/tagout per SOP-P2-L2-05 and confirm zero-energy state.
3. Access thermocouple junctions using panels identified in MM-P2-L2-HT02-S1.
4. Inspect thermocouple wiring and connectors for continuity and mechanical integrity. Replace components showing signs of wear or damage in accordance with MM-P2-L2-HT02-S1.
5. Calibrate the thermocouples using the calibration reference standard. The thermocouple calibration interval for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L2-HT02) is 40 days. Record calibration results in the equipment log.
6. Verify controller configuration and setpoints. The austenitizing setpoint for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L2-HT02) is 855 °C. Confirm controller reads within tolerance of the calibrated thermocouple per plant calibration procedure in MM-P2-L2-HT02-S1.
7. Reassemble access panels, remove lockout/tagout devices, and return equipment to service following SOP-P2-L2-05.

Acceptance criteria
- Thermocouple calibration completed and logged at the specified interval: 40 days.
- Controller displays and records the austenitizing setpoint as 855 °C and tracks process temperature consistent with calibration results.
- No damaged thermocouple wiring or connectors remain installed.
- All steps documented in the equipment maintenance log and referenced to MM-P2-L2-HT02-S1, SOP-P2-L2-02, and SOP-P2-L2-05.
title: Maintenance manual - Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #2

# MM-P2-L2-RR03 - Maintenance manual - Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #3

Revision: Rev A  
Plant: P2, line P2-L2  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L2-RR03

Scope
- This manual describes required preventive maintenance and adjustment steps for Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #3 (EQ-P2-L2-RR03). Follow referenced procedures SB-1049, SOP-P2-L2-03, and SOP-P2-L2-05 for safety and lockout/tagout requirements.

Tools
- Torque wrench calibrated to cover 620 N·m.
- Standard hand tools and inspection mirror.
- Grease gun compatible with machine fittings.
- Bearing inspection dye and lint-free wipes.
- Personal protective equipment per SB-1049.

Procedure
- Verify machine is de-energized per SOP-P2-L2-03 and locked out per SOP-P2-L2-05.
- Inspect visible surfaces of EQ-P2-L2-RR03 for wear, cracks, or oil leaks; clean as required.
- Check mandrel clamp fasteners for play. Apply specified tightening sequence and set mandrel clamp bolt torque. The mandrel clamp bolt torque for Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #3 (EQ-P2-L2-RR03) is 620 N·m.
- Access main roll bearing lubrication fittings. Remove dust caps and inspect threads and seals for damage. Apply grease until seals show fresh lubricant and excess is purged per grease gun guidance.
- Record lubrication event and runtime since last service. The main roll bearing lubrication interval for Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #3 (EQ-P2-L2-RR03) is 185 hours. Schedule next service accordingly.
- Reinstall guards and perform a low-speed function check per SOP-P2-L2-03. Confirm no abnormal noise or vibration before returning machine to production.

Acceptance criteria
- All mandrel clamp bolts achieve the specified torque without evidence of thread stripping or washer deformation.
- Main roll bearings receive lubricant and show no signs of metal contamination or significant leakage after the grease purge.
- Post-maintenance functional test shows normal operation with no abnormal noise, vibration, or temperature rise.
- Maintenance activity documented and cross-referenced to SB-1049, SOP-P2-L2-03, and SOP-P2-L2-05 in the equipment log.
title: Maintenance manual - Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #3

# MM-P2-L3-RR01 - Maintenance manual - Machining radial ring rolling mill #1

Revision: Rev C  
Plant: P2, line P2-L3  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L3-RR01

Scope
This document defines preventive maintenance tasks and acceptance criteria for machining radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P2-L3-RR01) to ensure safe, repeatable operation of the machining cell. Apply in conjunction with procedures and change notices cited in Related Documents.

Tools
- Adjustable torque wrench capable of 470 N·m
- Bearing grease gun and compatible grease fittings
- Standard set of hand tools and inspection mirror
- Clean lint-free rags and inspection light
- Personal protective equipment per plant standard

Procedure
- Isolate and lock out the equipment energy sources per SOP-P2-L3-01 before any maintenance entry.
- Inspect visible fasteners, guards, and hose routing for wear or damage. Clean contact surfaces and remove debris from the machining area.
- For mandrel clamp maintenance: position the mandrel per machine procedure, and tighten mandrel clamp bolts to 470 N·m using a calibrated torque wrench. Verify bolt seating and clamp alignment visually.
- Lubrication task: service the main roll bearings using the specified grease and fittings. Perform lubrication at the interval of 165 hours of machine operation. Record machine hours and lubrication events in the equipment log.
- Reassemble guards and remove lockout only after verifying all tools and loose items are cleared. Test run per SOP-P2-L3-03 to confirm normal operation.

Acceptance criteria
- Mandrel clamp bolts remain at torque of 470 N·m and show no evidence of loosening or thread damage.
- Main roll bearings show proper grease distribution and no signs of overheating, leakage, or metal contamination after lubrication at the 165 hours interval.
- No abnormal vibrations, noises, or tool runout beyond operator-permissible limits detected during test run per SOP-P2-L3-03.
- Maintenance actions and verifications are recorded in the equipment log and referenced to ECN-2026-018 where applicable.

Related Documents
- ECN-2026-018
- SOP-P2-L3-01
- SOP-P2-L3-03
title: Maintenance manual - Machining radial ring rolling mill #1

# MM-P2-L3-HT02 - Maintenance manual - Machining heat treat furnace #2

Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P2, line P2-L3  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L3-HT02

Scope
This document defines preventive maintenance and verification tasks for Machining heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L3-HT02). Activities cover control setpoint verification, thermocouple calibration, visual inspection, and basic corrective actions required to maintain process stability and product conformity. Refer to SB-1023, SB-1045, and SOP-P2-L3-03 for related procedures and safety requirements.

Tools
- Hand tools suitable for panel access and terminal checks
- Insulated thermocouple connector kit
- Calibration reference thermometer and traceable calibration certificate
- Personal protective equipment per SOP-P2-L3-03

Procedure
- Prepare the furnace for maintenance in accordance with SOP-P2-L3-03 and lockout/tagout requirements cited in SB-1023.
- Verify the control austenitizing setpoint for Machining heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L3-HT02) at the control interface. The austenitizing setpoint for Machining heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L3-HT02) is 845 °C. Confirm displayed value matches documented setpoint.
- Perform thermocouple integrity check and functional test against the calibration reference thermometer. The thermocouple calibration interval for Machining heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L3-HT02) is 50 days; record the calibration event and next due date in the equipment maintenance record.
- Inspect furnace interior, door seals, insulation condition, and control wiring for signs of degradation. Report findings per SB-1045.
- Restore furnace to service following verification steps and document any deviations and corrective actions in the maintenance log.

- Control interface shows the austenitizing setpoint for Machining heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L3-HT02) as 845 °C.

text:
# MM-P2-L3-IH03 - Maintenance manual - Machining induction billet heater #3

Revision: Rev C  
Plant: P2, line P2-L3  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L3-IH03

Scope
- This manual covers preventive and corrective maintenance tasks required for Machining induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P2-L3-IH03) installed in P2-L3.
- Intended for qualified maintenance technicians and engineers responsible for heater mechanical, electrical, and cooling subsystems.
- Reference related procedures and quality requirements: MM-P2-L3-IH03-S3, QS-PROC-10, SOP-P2-L3-02.

Tools
- Insulated hand tools rated for the plant electrical policy.
- Thermal contact pyrometer or calibrated thermocouple capable of reading the target billet temperature.
- Flow meter compatible with the coil cooling water circuit.
- Personal protective equipment as specified in SOP-P2-L3-02.

Procedure
- Isolate power and verify lockout/tagout per plant practice before accessing the heater assembly; follow electrical isolation in SOP-P2-L3-02.
- Inspect coil and refractory visually for cracks, deformation, or loose fittings. Replace or report per MM-P2-L3-IH03-S3.
- Verify coil cooling water flow using the flow meter at the pump discharge or coil inlet. Confirm the coil cooling water flow minimum for Machining induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P2-L3-IH03) is 72 L/min. If flow is below this value, investigate strainers, valves, and pump performance; do not operate the heater until flow meets the specified minimum.
- With safe access and protective equipment, perform a heat-up verification on a test billet or instrumented surrogate. Confirm the target billet temperature for Machining induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P2-L3-IH03) is 1175 °C during process verification. If the target is not achieved, follow diagnostic steps in MM-P2-L3-IH03-S3.
- Reassemble covers and restore power following SOP-P2-L3-02. Record all findings and corrective actions in maintenance log per QS-PROC-10.

Acceptance criteria
- No visible damage or loose components on coil and refractory documented.
- Coil cooling water flow meets or exceeds 72 L/min.
- Heater achieves and maintains 1175 °C on verification billet within process control limits.
- All maintenance actions logged and referenced per MM-P2-L3-IH03-S3 and QS-PROC-10.

# MM-P2-L4-RR01 - Maintenance manual - Heat Treat radial ring rolling mill #1

Revision: Rev C  
Plant: P2, line P2-L4  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L4-RR01

Scope
This document defines routine maintenance actions for Heat Treat radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P2-L4-RR01). It covers required tools, stepwise procedure for mandrel clamp bolt check and main roll bearing lubrication, and acceptance criteria. Refer to SOP-P2-L4-02, SOP-P2-L4-03, and SOP-P2-L4-04 for related operating and safety instructions.

Tools
- Torque wrench calibrated for 525 N·m
- Grease gun compatible with specified bearing fittings
- Clean lint-free rags and approved shop solvent
- Personal protective equipment per SOP-P2-L4-03

Procedure
- Isolate energy sources and lock out following SOP-P2-L4-03 before any intervention.
- Inspect mandrel clamp assembly for visible damage or contamination. Clean surfaces with approved solvent and dry with lint-free rags.
- Set torque wrench to the mandrel clamp bolt torque for Heat Treat radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P2-L4-RR01) is 525 N·m and apply torque to each clamp bolt in a cross pattern until wrench indicates achieved value.
- After clamping, cycle the clamp mechanism manually to verify smooth operation without binding. If binding occurs, re-inspect components against SOP-P2-L4-02.
- Lubricate main roll bearings using the grease gun until fresh grease appears at seals and fittings. The main roll bearing lubrication interval for Heat Treat radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P2-L4-RR01) is 195 hours; record lubrication action in the equipment log per SOP-P2-L4-04.
- Remove lockout/tagout and return machine to service following checks in SOP-P2-L4-03.

Acceptance criteria
- Mandrel clamp bolts are secure and set to the mandrel clamp bolt torque for Heat Treat radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P2-L4-RR01) is 525 N·m.
- Main roll bearings show clean grease extrusion at fittings and no evidence of leakage or overheating during initial run.
- Maintenance entry recorded and cites SOP-P2-L4-02, SOP-P2-L4-03, SOP-P2-L4-04.
title: Maintenance manual - Heat Treat radial ring rolling mill #1

# MM-P2-L4-HT02 - Maintenance manual - Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2

Revision: Rev E  
Plant: P2, line P2-L4  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L4-HT02

## Scope
This document covers routine maintenance and verification tasks for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L4-HT02). It applies to operations and maintenance personnel responsible for safe operation and process control within line P2-L4. See SB-1016 for safety bulletin and hazards.

## Tools
- Calibrated thermocouple simulator
- Standard electrical hand tools per site kit
- Insulation inspection mirror
- Data logger compatible with furnace output
Refer to SOP-P2-L4-02 and SOP-P2-L4-03 for permitted tool lists and PPE requirements.

## Procedure
1. Verify lockout/tagout in accordance with SB-1016 before any access to EQ-P2-L4-HT02.
2. Visually inspect chamber interior and heating elements for damage. Record findings in maintenance log referenced in SOP-P2-L4-02.
3. Confirm control setpoint: The austenitizing setpoint for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L4-HT02) is 885 °C. Do not adjust without authorization from heat treat engineer per SOP-P2-L4-03.
4. Validate thermocouple response using the calibrated thermocouple simulator. Compare simulator output to furnace controller readout and document variance in the calibration section of the maintenance record.
5. Schedule and document calibration: The thermocouple calibration interval for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L4-HT02) is 55 days. Enter next due date in the maintenance management system immediately after completing calibration.
6. Verify data logger operation and confirm logged temperatures match controller output over a test cycle. Attach exported data to the maintenance record as required by SOP-P2-L4-02.
7. Restore power and remove lockout/tagout following SB-1016 procedures. Notify operations per SOP-P2-L4-03.

## Acceptance criteria
- Control readout setpoint is 885 °C and matches documented setpoint for EQ-P2-L4-HT02.
- Thermocouple meets calibration tolerance as recorded; next calibration scheduled per 55 days interval for EQ-P2-L4-HT02.
- No critical defects or safety items outstanding. Maintenance records complete and linked to SOP-P2-L4-02, SOP-P2-L4-03, and SB-1016.
title: Maintenance manual - Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2

# MM-P2-L4-HP03 - Maintenance manual - Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #3

Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P2, line P2-L4

Scope
- This manual covers routine maintenance and verification tasks required to maintain safe operation of the Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #3 (EQ-P2-L4-HP03). It applies to maintenance technicians and shift engineers performing mechanical and hydraulic inspections and adjustments.

Tools
- Standard hand tools and calibrated torque wrench capable of applying the specified bolt torque.  
- Hydraulic system test gauge and pressure-rated hoses compatible with system service ports.  
- Personal protective equipment per site policy.

Procedure
- Isolate and lock out EQ-P2-L4-HP03 per SOP-P2-L4-01 before any work begins. Follow machine-specific isolation points and tagout procedures referenced in SOP-P2-L4-01.  
- Perform a visual inspection of hydraulic lines, fittings, and the main ram for signs of leakage, wear, or damage. If any abnormal condition is found, stop and escalate per ECN-2026-042.  
- Verify system pressure using the hydraulic system test gauge at the recommended service port. Confirm the system pressure limit for Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #3 (EQ-P2-L4-HP03) is 320 bar. Do not operate the press above this pressure.  
- Tighten the main ram bolt to the specified value. The main ram bolt torque for Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #3 (EQ-P2-L4-HP03) is 1575 N·m. Use a calibrated torque wrench and follow the bolt manufacturer’s tightening sequence if available.  
- After adjustments, bleed the hydraulic system per established practice and remove isolation following SOP-P2-L4-01. Return the press to service only when all systems are verified functional and no leaks are present.

Acceptance criteria
- No hydraulic leaks at fittings, hoses, or ram seals under the system pressure limit for Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #3 (EQ-P2-L4-HP03) of 320 bar.  
- Main ram bolt torqued to the main ram bolt torque for Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #3 (EQ-P2-L4-HP03) of 1575 N·m as verified on a calibrated torque wrench.  
- All lockout/tagout steps completed and documented per SOP-P2-L4-01. Any deviations must be reported and managed per ECN-2026-042 and SB-1007.

- SB-1007

text:
# MM-P3-L1-HP01 - Maintenance manual - Hot Forge hydraulic forging press #1

Revision: Rev B  
Plant: P3, line P3-L1  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L1-HP01

## Scope
This document defines the maintenance procedure for Hot Forge hydraulic forging press EQ-P3-L1-HP01. It covers routine mechanical and hydraulic checks required to verify safe operation and to return the press to service following planned maintenance. Refer to MM-P3-L1-HP01-S1 for the inspection checklist and to SOP-P3-L1-01 and SOP-P3-L1-02 for operator and lockout/tagout procedures.

## Tools
- Fixed and adjustable wrenches sized to match fasteners on EQ-P3-L1-HP01
- Torque wrench capable of applying the main ram bolt torque for Hot Forge hydraulic forging press #1 (EQ-P3-L1-HP01) is 1425 N·m
- Pressure gauge calibrated for system verification up to the system pressure limit for Hot Forge hydraulic forging press #1 (EQ-P3-L1-HP01) is 330 bar
- Hydraulic fluid handling kit and drip containment
- Clean lint-free rags and visual inspection mirror

## Procedure
- Isolate EQ-P3-L1-HP01 per SOP-P3-L1-01 and SOP-P3-L1-02 before any maintenance.
- Drain and contain hydraulic fluid following plant environmental practices; inspect reservoir and filters using MM-P3-L1-HP01-S1.
- Visually inspect ram assembly, hose runs, fittings, and structural fasteners for wear or damage.
- Re-torque main ram bolts to the main ram bolt torque for Hot Forge hydraulic forging press #1 (EQ-P3-L1-HP01) is 1425 N·m using the calibrated torque wrench. Torque sequence: follow manufacturer flange pattern documented in MM-P3-L1-HP01-S1.
- Refill and purge hydraulic system, then verify system pressure does not exceed the system pressure limit for Hot Forge hydraulic forging press #1 (EQ-P3-L1-HP01) is 330 bar using the calibrated pressure gauge.

# MM-P3-L1-IH03 - Maintenance manual - Hot Forge induction billet heater #3

Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P3, line P3-L1  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L1-IH03

## Scope
This document covers maintenance tasks required to verify operation and safety of Hot Forge induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P3-L1-IH03). Tasks include inspection of electrical connections, coil cooling water system verification, control system health check, and confirmation of billet heating performance. Reference applicable safety bulletins and operating procedures: SB-1044, SB-1047, SOP-P3-L1-05.

## Tools
- Insulated hand tools suitable for industrial electrical work  
- Portable thermal sensor or pyrometer capable of reading target billet temperature  
- Flow meter compatible with coil cooling water circuit  
- Personal protective equipment per SOP-P3-L1-05

## Procedure
- Isolate equipment per SOP-P3-L1-05 and verify lockout/tagout compliance before any maintenance access.  
- Inspect coil assembly for signs of damage, wear, or loose fittings. Confirm electrical connections are clean and secure.  
- Restore power and perform control system diagnostics guided by SB-1044 and SB-1047. Verify alarms and interlocks function per manufacturer guidance.  
- Measure coil cooling water flow using the flow meter at the coil inlet and outlet locations. Confirm measured flow meets or exceeds the coil cooling water flow minimum for Hot Forge induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P3-L1-IH03): 65 L/min.  
- Run a heating cycle with a test billet following SOP-P3-L1-05. Monitor billet temperature using the portable thermal sensor or pyrometer. Confirm heating profile achieves the target billet temperature for Hot Forge induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P3-L1-IH03): 1260 °C.  
- If any parameter fails to meet acceptance criteria, tag component out of service and escalate per SB-1044.

## Acceptance criteria
- Coil cooling water flow equals or exceeds 65 L/min.  
- Billet reaches 1260 °C under normal operating control conditions as defined in SOP-P3-L1-05.  
- No active electrical faults or unaddressed mechanical defects remain.  
- All tests and corrective actions documented and filed per plant document control.
title: Maintenance manual - Hot Forge induction billet heater #3

# MM-P3-L2-SB01 Maintenance manual - Ring Rolling shot blast cabinet #1

Revision: Rev A  
Plant: P3, line P3-L2  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L2-SB01

Scope
This document defines routine maintenance tasks for the Ring Rolling shot blast cabinet EQ-P3-L2-SB01. It covers inspection, wear components replacement, media top-up, and mechanical fastener verification required to maintain safe and effective operation. Refer to ECN-2026-019 for change history and configuration baseline.

Tools
- Adjustable lifting strap and hoist suitable for cabinet access
- Torque wrench calibrated per facility practice
- Hand tools and fastener access set compatible with cabinet hardware
- Personal protective equipment as specified in SOP-P3-L2-01 and SOP-P3-L2-05

Procedure
Perform maintenance only after isolation and lockout in accordance with SOP-P3-L2-01. Verify cabinet is depressurized and power is isolated. Inspect cabinet interior for liner wear and foreign material. Remove worn liner panels following removal sequence in the cabinet access procedure in SOP-P3-L2-05. When reinstalling liner panels, clean mating surfaces and clamp panels to prevent movement during torqueing.

Fastener verification: tighten blast wheel liner bolts to the specified torque. The blast wheel liner bolt torque for Ring Rolling shot blast cabinet #1 (EQ-P3-L2-SB01) is 100 N·m. Use a calibrated torque wrench and apply torque in a cross pattern to distribute load evenly.

Shot media: check media quality and contamination. Replenish media when level and performance indicate attrition. The shot media top-up interval for Ring Rolling shot blast cabinet #1 (EQ-P3-L2-SB01) is 40 hours. Record media additions in the maintenance log and dispose of contaminated media per SOP-P3-L2-05.

Finalize maintenance by securing access panels and restoring normal energy following SOP-P3-L2-01. Run a verification cycle to confirm blast pattern and cabinet integrity before returning to production.

Acceptance criteria
- Liner panels secure with blast wheel liner bolts torqued to 100 N·m.  
- No visible cracks, distortions, or loose components inside the cabinet after maintenance.  
- Shot media level and condition meet operational requirements following the shot media top-up interval of 40 hours and documentation completed in the maintenance log.  
- Post-maintenance verification cycle demonstrates acceptable blast performance.  

Related documents: ECN-2026-019, SOP-P3-L2-01, SOP-P3-L2-05
title: Maintenance manual - Ring Rolling shot blast cabinet #1

Scope

# MM-P3-L2-HT03 - Maintenance manual - Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #3

Revision: Rev B  
Plant: P3, line P3-L2  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L2-HT03

Scope
This manual covers routine preventive maintenance and verification steps for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P3-L2-HT03). It is limited to mechanical, electrical visual inspection and thermocouple calibration activities required to maintain process control and safe operation. Refer to SB-1015, SB-1041, and SOP-P3-L2-01 for related safety bulletins and operational procedures.

Tools
- Insulated hand tools appropriate for high-temperature equipment
- Thermocouple simulator compatible with furnace control module
- Handheld infrared thermometer for surface checks
- Personal protective equipment as specified in SOP-P3-L2-01

Procedure
- Prepare: Verify lockout/tagout per SOP-P3-L2-01 before accessing panels or sensors. Confirm cooldown to ambient following plant procedures in SB-1015.
- Visual inspection: Inspect chamber seals, door latches, and external wiring for damage or contamination. Clean lint and debris from door seals and air intakes using non-sparking tools.
- Thermocouple verification: Remove access cover for sensor harness. Connect thermocouple simulator and compare readback to simulator output at multiple points across the expected operating range. Adjust controller linearization if deviation exceeds acceptance criteria.
- Setpoint verification: Confirm controller displays and logs the austenitizing setpoint for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P3-L2-HT03) as 870 °C. Escalate discrepancies to maintenance supervision and log per SB-1041.
- Reassembly: Secure all covers and restore power. Perform a controlled heat cycle as required by SOP-P3-L2-01 to confirm stable control response.

Acceptance criteria
- Thermocouple calibration interval for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P3-L2-HT03) is 55 days. Calibration records must show completion within that interval.
- Controller displays the austenitizing setpoint as 870 °C and maintains stable control during verification cycle.
- No physical damage or unsafe conditions remain after maintenance. All actions documented per SB-1041 and SOP-P3-L2-01.
title: Maintenance manual - Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #3

# MM-P3-L3-HP03 Maintenance manual - Machining hydraulic forging press #3

Revision: Rev E  
Plant: P3, line P3-L3

## Scope
This document covers preventative and corrective maintenance tasks for Machining hydraulic forging press #3 (EQ-P3-L3-HP03) located in P3, line P3-L3. Tasks include inspection, fastener verification, hydraulic system verification, and functional checks. Refer to SB-1011 for safety bulletin and to SOP-P3-L3-02 and SOP-P3-L3-03 for lockout/tagout and routine operation steps.

- Calibrated torque wrench capable of 1600 N·m.  
- Hydraulic pressure gauge compatible with system fittings.  
- Standard mechanic hand tools and lifting gear per SB-1011.  
- Personal protective equipment as specified in SB-1011.

## Procedure
1. Prepare unit for maintenance following SOP-P3-L3-02 for lockout/tagout and SOP-P3-L3-03 for safe handling.  
2. Visually inspect ram, cylinder body, hoses, and fittings for leaks, damage, or misalignment. Document findings.  
3. Verify and test hydraulic system pressure with the hydraulic pressure gauge. Confirm the system pressure limit for Machining hydraulic forging press #3 (EQ-P3-L3-HP03) is 295 bar. Do not exceed this limit during testing.  
4. Torque main ram fasteners: the main ram bolt torque for Machining hydraulic forging press #3 (EQ-P3-L3-HP03) is 1600 N·m. Apply torque in the sequence per manufacturer flange pattern; use calibrated torque equipment.  
5. After adjustments, cycle the press at low pressure per SOP-P3-L3-03 to confirm proper motion and absence of leaks. Monitor system for abnormal noise or behavior.

## Acceptance criteria
- No hydraulic leaks present at cylinder, fittings, or hoses after cycling.  
- System pressure does not exceed the system pressure limit for Machining hydraulic forging press #3 (EQ-P3-L3-HP03) is 295 bar during normal operation and testing.  
- Main ram fasteners are torqued to the main ram bolt torque for Machining hydraulic forging press #3 (EQ-P3-L3-HP03) is 1600 N·m, verified with calibration record.  
- All safety devices and interlocks operational per SB-1011 and SOP-P3-L3-02/SOP-P3-L3-03.

Scope
- Routine maintenance and verification procedures for Heat Treat radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P3-L4-RR01) to ensure safe operation and consistent product quality during heat treat downstream operations.
- Refer to SB-1028 for safety boundaries and lockout/tagout requirements prior to maintenance activities.

- Bearing lubrication pump and manufacturer-recommended lubricant.
- Standard hand tools and inspection mirror.
- Personal protective equipment per SB-1028 and SOP-P3-L4-02.

- Isolate and lock out the mill per SB-1028 before any maintenance. Verify isolation with authorized personnel as directed in SOP-P3-L4-02.
- Inspect mandrel clamp assembly for wear, cracks, and secure fasteners. The mandrel clamp bolt torque for Heat Treat radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P3-L4-RR01) is 605 N·m.

Acceptance criteria
- Mandrel clamp bolts achieve and hold the specified torque without evidence of slippage or loosening.
- Main roll bearings show reduced contamination, proper lubricant presence, and no abnormal noise or vibration following procedure.

This manual describes required maintenance actions for EQ-P3-L4-HT02 to ensure safe, repeatable heat treat cycles and compliance with plant quality procedures. Refer to ECN-2026-001 for configuration changes and to SOP-P3-L4-02 and SOP-P3-L4-05 for operational and safety procedures.

# MM-P1-L4-CN01-S2 Fastener inspection and torque - Heat Treat CNC turning center #1
Revision: Rev C
Plant: P1, line P1-L4
Equipment: EQ-P1-L4-CN01

## Scope
This document defines the fastener inspection and lubrication verification procedure for Heat Treat CNC turning center #1 (EQ-P1-L4-CN01). It covers visual inspection, verification of thread engagement, and confirmation of lube refill interval and lubricant part number. For machine operation and safety referencing, see SOP-P1-L4-03, SOP-P1-L4-04, SOP-P1-L4-05.

## Tools
- Torque wrench (appropriate range for machine fasteners; use calibrated tool in calibration program)
- Thread gage set or engagement verification tool
- Clean lint-free rags and inspection light
- Parts cleaner and rust inhibitor as required
- Replacement lubricant: CFW-LUB-477.

## Procedure
- Isolate power and tag out per SOP-P1-L4-03 before any access to guarded areas.
- Open access panels following machine-specific access points in SOP-P1-L4-04.
- Inspect all externally accessible fasteners for looseness, corrosion, stripped heads, and missing hardware. Verify full thread engagement at each joint; note any excessive play.
- If a fastener is found loose, remove, clean the mating surfaces, apply appropriate thread treatment if specified in SOP-P1-L4-05, and reassemble using the calibrated torque wrench. Record action in maintenance history.
- Verify lubricant reservoir and service records. The way lube refill interval for Heat Treat CNC turning center #1 (EQ-P1-L4-CN01) is 40 hours.
- Confirm lubricant part number in the reservoir and stores matches CFW-LUB-477.
- Restore panels and remove lockout following SOP-P1-L4-03. Run functional verification per SOP-P1-L4-04.

## Acceptance criteria
- No fasteners are found loose, damaged, or missing after corrective action.
- Thread engagement is verified and within acceptable fit per manufacturer guidance referenced in SOP-P1-L4-05.
- Way lube refill records confirm adherence to the way lube refill interval for Heat Treat CNC turning center #1 (EQ-P1-L4-CN01) is 40 hours.
- Reservoir contains lubricant part number CFW-LUB-477 and records are updated.

Scope

Scope

- Verify quench system timers and interlocks in coordination with operations. The quench delay maximum for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P1-L2-HT03) is 24 seconds. Document verification results and return system to service per SOP-P1-L2-01.

- Quench delay verified at or below the quench delay maximum for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P1-L2-HT03) is 24 seconds.

# MM-P2-L4-HT02-S2 Fastener inspection and torque - Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2

Revision: Rev B  
Plant: P2, line P2-L4  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L4-HT02

Scope
- This document prescribes fastener inspection and torque verification for EQ-P2-L4-HT02. Use this procedure between scheduled maintenance activities and after any intervention that disturbs fastened joints. Refer to MM-P2-L4-HT02 and SOP-P2-L4-01 for overarching maintenance planning and to SOP-P2-L4-04 for lockout/tagout requirements.

Tools
- Calibrated hand torque wrench suitable for specified torque values (use manufacturer or referenced documentation for target values).  
- Quick-reference fastener checklist.  
- Inspection mirror and flashlight.  
- Clean lint-free rags and solvent approved by maintenance.  
- Lubricant: CFW-LUB-426.

Procedure
- Prepare: Verify LOTO per SOP-P2-L4-04 and confirm scope with maintenance planner per MM-P2-L4-HT02.  
- Visual inspection: Inspect all exposed fasteners for corrosion, thread damage, washers condition, and evidence of movement or fretting. Document findings on the checklist.  
- Clean and prepare: Remove debris and old lubricant from mating surfaces using approved solvent. Apply lubricant CFW-LUB-426 where specified by the fastener manufacturer or referenced documentation.  
- Torque sequence: Follow the torque sequence and values provided in the equipment manufacturer documentation or MM-P2-L4-HT02. Use a calibrated torque wrench and apply torque in consistent increments until final values are achieved. If any fastener does not achieve required torque, document and replace the fastener per MM-P2-L4-HT02.  
- Special note: Do not operate EQ-P2-L4-HT02 until fastener condition is verified and documented. Observe quench system guidance; the quench delay maximum for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L4-HT02) is 10 seconds.

Acceptance criteria
- All inspected fasteners show no visual defects and meet the specified torque values per MM-P2-L4-HT02.  
- Lubricant applied where required: CFW-LUB-426 documented.  
- Checklist completed and signed; any deviations routed to maintenance planner and recorded per SOP-P2-L4-01.

# MM-P1-L4-HT03-S3 Calibration checks - Heat Treat heat treat furnace #3

Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P1, line P1-L4  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L4-HT03

Scope
- This document defines the calibration check procedure for sensors and timing functions on Heat Treat heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P1-L4-HT03). Follow referenced process controls and safety steps in MM-P1-L4-HT03 and SOP-P1-L4-02, SOP-P1-L4-03.

- Traceable verification tags and log forms as specified in MM-P1-L4-HT03.

Procedure
1. Verify authorization and lockout per SOP-P1-L4-02 before accessing controller terminals.  
2. Confirm power-off and safe condition per SOP-P1-L4-03.  
3. Inspect physical condition of sensors and connections per MM-P1-L4-HT03. Replace or repair only with parts and procedures listed in MM-P1-L4-HT03.  
4. Connect calibrated test instrument to the sensor terminal. Perform zero and span checks following the instrument vendor procedure and the calibration checkpoints in MM-P1-L4-HT03. Record measured values on the calibration log.  
5. Verify timing control relay and digital timer outputs against expected response. When measuring the quench activation timing, record measured delay and compare to acceptance limits. The quench delay maximum for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P1-L4-HT03) is 15 seconds.  
6. If adjustment is required, adjust per MM-P1-L4-HT03 and recheck. Apply lubricant where required using CFW-LUB-231 and document in maintenance record.  
7. Restore system to operational status per SOP-P1-L4-03 and update calibration tag and records.

Acceptance criteria
- All sensors and timers meet setpoint agreement and functional response defined in MM-P1-L4-HT03.  
- Measured quench delay is within the limit: The quench delay maximum for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P1-L4-HT03) is 15 seconds.  
- Lubrication recorded using The lubricant part number for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P1-L4-HT03) is CFW-LUB-231.

Scope

- Oil drain pan suitable for contaminant control
- Oil cartridge funnel or approved dispensing nozzle
- Personal protective equipment as required by site SOPs

- No external leakage from filler cap or seals after refill.

## Scope
This document describes the required fastener inspection and torque verification process for Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #3 (EQ-P2-L2-RR03). Revision: Rev B  
Plant: P3, line P3-L4

Scope
- This procedure defines calibration check activities for Heat Treat radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P3-L4-RR01) to verify geometric and control-system alignment before production of rings up to the maximum ring outer diameter for Heat Treat radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P3-L4-RR01) is 1720 mm. Use this document in conjunction with SOP-P3-L4-02, SOP-P3-L4-03, and SOP-P3-L4-05.

Tools
- Dial indicators with magnetic bases suitable for mill spindle and carriage checks.  
- Straightedge and feeler gauges for guide way inspection.  
- Handheld alignment laser or optical target compatible with mill datum points.  
- Cleaning supplies and approved lubricant part number CFW-LUB-315.  
- Calibration log form from document control.

Procedure
- Prepare the machine following SOP-P3-L4-02 for lockout and safe access.  
- Clean measurement surfaces and datum faces per SOP-P3-L4-03.  
- Mount the alignment laser or optical target on the primary spindle datum and reference the carriage datum. Record relative positional offsets on the calibration log form.  
- Verify guide way straightness with the straightedge and feeler gauges along the working length; document any deviations found.  
- Check spindle runout with dial indicators on the intended ring mounting flange and record results. Use the calibration log form to capture each measurement and any corrective actions.  
- Apply lubricant where required before reassembly using lubricant part number CFW-LUB-315 per lubrication points specified in SOP-P3-L4-05.  
- Release machine from maintenance state following SOP-P3-L4-02 and confirm control setpoints are restored.

Acceptance criteria
- All documented measurement results must be within machine design allowances as specified in the equipment calibration baseline.  
- Any measurement outside baseline must be recorded, corrected, and rechecked before production of rings approaching the maximum ring outer diameter for Heat Treat radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P3-L4-RR01) is 1720 mm.  
- Calibration log form must reference SOP-P3-L4-02, SOP-P3-L4-03, and SOP-P3-L4-05 and be filed in the equipment maintenance record.

Scope
This document describes calibration verification checks for Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #2 (EQ-P3-L1-SB02) following startup and after major maintenance. Checks focus on measurement systems and alarms that affect shot delivery, media recycling, and dust collection performance. Refer to SOP-P3-L1-02, SOP-P3-L1-04, and SOP-P3-L1-05 for related operational and safety procedures.

- Non-marring alignment probes and feeler gauge set
- Supply of lubricant: CFW-LUB-278

- Visually inspect cabinet interior and media recycling components for wear or foreign material. Record observations on the calibration tag.

- Apply CFW-LUB-278 to specified mechanical bearings and linkage points where lubrication notes exist in the equipment history. Record lubricant serial or batch reference.

Acceptance criteria
- All instrument and alarm points return nominal readings and are mechanically secure.
- The dust collector pressure drop alarm for Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #2 (EQ-P3-L1-SB02) is set to and verified as 2025 Pa.

- Lubricant: CFW-LUB-188

Procedure
1. Secure equipment per SOP-P1-L1-03 and confirm line isolation using SOP-P1-L1-05.
2. Perform visual inspection of the heating coil assembly. Note any deformation, discoloration, or conductive debris and record findings in the maintenance log.
3. Verify sensor outputs at their harness connectors with the multimeter. Compare readings to baseline recorded in MM-P1-L1-IH03.
4. Check insulation resistance on primary and secondary conductors with the insulation resistance tester. Document results in the calibration record.
5. Inspect connectors and cable terminations for corrosion or looseness. Re-seat connectors as required and clean contact surfaces with approved electrical contact cleaner.
6. Apply lubricant CFW-LUB-188 to designated mechanical linkages per details in MM-P1-L1-IH03.
7. Restore power and observe startup behavior. Record any alarms, fault codes, or deviations from baseline performance documented in MM-P1-L1-IH03.

Acceptance criteria
- No visible coil damage or contamination per visual inspection.
- Sensor outputs match baseline entries in MM-P1-L1-IH03 within allowable tolerance stated in that document.
- Insulation resistance measurements meet the minimums recorded in MM-P1-L1-IH03.
- Connectors and terminations show secure contact and no corrosion after cleaning.
- Lubricant CFW-LUB-188 applied where specified.
- Coil inspection interval for Hot Forge induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P1-L1-IH03) is 290 hours.
title: Calibration checks - Hot Forge induction billet heater #3

Scope

# MM-P3-L2-HT03-S3 Calibration checks - Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #3

Revision: Rev C  
Plant: P3, line P3-L2  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L2-HT03

## Scope
This document defines calibration check steps for sensors and timing on Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P3-L2-HT03). Checks cover timing verification, sensor functional confirmation, and lubrication verification required to support heat treat process control. See related change history and baseline procedures in ECN-2026-017 and MM-P3-L2-HT03. Refer to SB-1041 for safety barriers and lockout-tagout supplements.

## Tools
- Calibrated timing indicator compatible with furnace control outputs.  
- Multimeter for continuity and signal verification.  
- Thermal sensor simulator or appropriate simulator per MM-P3-L2-HT03.  
- Manufacturer-approved lubricant: CFW-LUB-159.  
- Standard PPE per SB-1041.

## Procedure
1. Secure furnace per SB-1041 and verify lockout-tagout.  
2. Power control cabinet to calibration mode as directed in MM-P3-L2-HT03.  
3. Using the timing indicator, trigger the control output that initiates quench sequence. Record the measured delay between command and quench valve actuation.  
4. Compare measured delay to the allowed quench delay maximum for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P3-L2-HT03). If measured delay exceeds the quench delay maximum for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P3-L2-HT03) is 13 seconds, follow the fault escalation steps in ECN-2026-017.  
5. Verify sensor outputs using the thermal sensor simulator; confirm reading stability and range per MM-P3-L2-HT03.  
6. Inspect and, if required by wear indicators, apply lubricant CFW-LUB-159 to specified mechanical linkages following manufacturer guidance. Document lubricant application in maintenance log.

## Acceptance criteria
- Timing check: recorded quench delay must be less than or equal to the quench delay maximum for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P3-L2-HT03) is 13 seconds.  
- All monitored sensors return stable readings within expected outputs documented in MM-P3-L2-HT03.  
- Lubrication applied as required using CFW-LUB-159 and logged.  
- Any failure or deviation triggers corrective actions per ECN-2026-017 and locks the equipment out per SB-1041 until resolved.
title: Calibration checks - Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #3

Scope

Follow associated work methods in SOP-P3-L3-01, SOP-P3-L3-03, and SOP-P3-L3-05.

text:
# SB-1001 — Safety bulletin: noise exposure

Revision: Rev E  
Plant: P2, line P2-L1  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L1-IH02

Hazard description
- Operators and maintenance personnel working at Hot Forge induction billet heater #2 (EQ-P2-L1-IH02) are exposed to elevated continuous and intermittent noise during routine charging, heating, and billet handling operations. Prolonged exposure can cause temporary or permanent hearing degradation and increases the risk of communication failures during critical lifts and equipment adjustments. Noise sources include induction cycle transitions, billet feed impacts, and material handling steps adjacent to the heater.

Affected equipment
- Primary: EQ-P2-L1-IH02 (Hot Forge induction billet heater #2). Target billet temperature for Hot Forge induction billet heater #2 (EQ-P2-L1-IH02) is 1180 °C.  
- Secondary: local material handling and feed systems associated with the EQ-P2-L1-IH02 work area. Refer to MM-P2-L1-IH02 for maintenance history and recent modifications that influence acoustic emissions.

Required controls
- Administrative: implement controlled access to the immediate work zone during active heating and charging cycles. Update shift briefings to emphasize noise hazards and communication signals specific to EQ-P2-L1-IH02. Review applicable procedures in SOP-P2-L1-01 and SOP-P2-L1-05 to ensure alignment of noise mitigation with operational steps and lockout/tagout practices.
- Personal protective equipment: require approved hearing protection for all personnel in the defined zone. Ensure fit-check and training per site PPE program before assignment to tasks with EQ-P2-L1-IH02.
- Engineering and work-practice: where feasible, schedule noisy operations when nonessential personnel are absent; use spot shielding and dampening at feed/impact points; prioritize vibration isolation during maintenance activities documented in MM-P2-L1-IH02.
- Verification: supervisors shall confirm compliance at shift start and record observations in line logs; escalate repeat exceedances to Maintenance and Safety for corrective action.

Effective date
- Effective date: Rev E. Review references MM-P2-L1-IH02, SOP-P2-L1-01, SOP-P2-L1-05 for related requirements and implementation details.
title: Safety bulletin: noise exposure

text:
# SB-1002 Safety bulletin: arc flash at the induction power cabinet

Revision: Rev C  
Plant: P2, line P2-L1  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L1-SB03

Hazard description
An arc flash event was observed originating from the induction power cabinet feeding the Hot Forge induction system adjacent to the shot blast area. The initiating sequence involved an electrical fault during routine operation which resulted in a localized flash and associated ejected particulate. Personnel in the immediate work area experienced near-miss exposure to thermal energy and flying debris. Contributing factors identified during the preliminary review include inadequate electrical isolation during work on adjacent systems and unexpected energization paths created by shared grounding and bonding conditions. The event highlights the potential for stored electrical energy to arc when maintenance, adjustments, or media handling activities are performed without verified isolation.

Affected equipment
Primary equipment implicated: induction power cabinet for the Hot Forge induction system and the adjacent shot media handling for Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #3. The shot media top-up interval for Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P2-L1-SB03) is 33 hours. Personnel and tools operating in the immediate cell, including contractors and maintenance staff, should consider the induction power cabinet and the shot blast media handling interfaces as potentially energized until isolation and verification are complete. See MM-P2-L1-SB03, SOP-P2-L1-03, SOP-P2-L1-04 for maintenance and operational history relevant to this bulletin.

Required controls
- Immediately restrict access to the induction power cabinet work area to qualified electrical personnel only until an electrical hazard assessment and isolation verification are completed.  
- Implement and enforce lockout/tagout and zero energy verification procedures before any work on or near the induction power cabinet or shot media handling equipment. Follow the procedures referenced in SOP-P2-L1-03 and SOP-P2-L1-04.  
- Perform a grounding and bonding inspection of the cabinet and adjacent structures and remediate any discontinuities identified. Document findings in MM-P2-L1-SB03.  
- Update permits and work planning to include specific arc flash and media handling interactions, and require arc-rated PPE when verification is not completed.

Effective date
This bulletin is effective immediately and remains in force until the corrective actions and verification activities identified in MM-P2-L1-SB03 are closed.
title: Safety bulletin: arc flash at the induction power cabinet

text:
# SB-1003 Safety bulletin: arc flash at the induction power cabinet

Revision: Rev A  
Plant: P2, line P2-L3  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L3-HT02

Hazard description
An arc flash incident occurred at the induction power cabinet on EQ-P2-L3-HT02 while performing routine inspection and thermocouple replacement activities. The event produced molten metal and an energy release within the cabinet enclosure, presenting burn and blast hazards to personnel performing work at the cabinet front and nearby. Root-cause analysis identified energized components exposed during inspection and inadequate isolation and grounding procedures during thermocouple handling as contributing factors. Personnel were protected by PPE but experienced minor thermal exposure; material and tooling sustained damage that required follow-up repair.

Affected equipment
This bulletin applies to EQ-P2-L3-HT02 (Machining heat treat furnace #2) and all associated induction power cabinets and harnessing on line P2-L3 at Plant P2. The thermocouple calibration interval for Machining heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L3-HT02) is 50 days. Technicians, maintenance, and operations personnel assigned to EQ-P2-L3-HT02 or performing work on its power cabinet must follow the required controls below.

Required controls
- De-energize and verify zero energy state at the induction power cabinet before opening the enclosure. Use applied verification per SOP-P2-L3-02.  
- Place lockout/tagout on all incoming power feeds and verify isolation continuity per MM-P2-L3-HT02.  
- Bond and ground thermocouple leads to chassis before disconnection and reconnection to prevent capacitive discharge. Document bonding actions in the maintenance record per MM-P2-L3-HT02-S3.  
- Restrict entry to a two-person team when any panel is open; second person must remain at a safe distance with communication line.  
- Use arc-rated PPE for exposures inside the cabinet boundary; conduct a pre-job briefing to confirm roles and emergency procedures.  
- Report all anomalies and near-misses using existing incident reporting channels and reference this bulletin and the cited documents for corrective tasks.

Effective date
Effective immediately upon release.
title: Safety bulletin: arc flash at the induction power cabinet

text:
# SB-1004 - Safety bulletin: airborne dust from blasting

Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P1, line P1-L4  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L4-HP02

Hazard description
- Operations adjacent to the blast booth on line P1-L4 are generating airborne particulate that migrates into the adjoining press room. Dust accumulation on machinery and in ventilation intakes presents respiratory and ignition hazards for operators and maintenance personnel. Secondary exposure routes include transfer of dust on clothing and tools into the heat treat area associated with EQ-P1-L4-HP02. Silicate- and metallic-containing particles can abrade seals and contaminate hydraulic systems if introduced during maintenance.

Affected equipment
- Primary: EQ-P1-L4-HP02 (Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #2). The lubricant part number for Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #2 (EQ-P1-L4-HP02) is CFW-LUB-195.
- Secondary: blasting booth enclosures, local extraction ducts, press-room ventilation intakes, and nearby tooling storage.

Required controls
- Administrative: restrict non-essential entry to the press room during blasting operations. Post warning signage at access points and include SB-1034, SOP-P1-L4-04, and SOP-P1-L4-05 in shift briefings.
- Engineering: verify integrity of seals on press-room doors and ensure blast booth curtains overlap to prevent forward migration. Increase local exhaust capture at source during blasting and confirm press-room ventilation is set to negative pressure relative to the blast booth when blasting is active.
- Housekeeping: implement targeted cleaning after each blast cycle at tool benches, ventilation grilles, and machine housings using HEPA-filtered vacuum only. Do not use compressed air for cleaning contaminated surfaces.
- PPE and hygiene: require NIOSH-approved particulate respirators where airborne concentrations are present, and provide change areas to prevent cross-contamination to the heat treat area. Launder or contain contaminated clothing on site.
- Maintenance: when performing work on EQ-P1-L4-HP02, inspect hydraulic reservoirs and suction screens for contamination prior to introducing lubricant CFW-LUB-195. Document inspection and any fluid contamination per SOP-P1-L4-05.

Effective date
- This bulletin is effective immediately upon issue. Review controls and training before the next blasting schedule.
title: Safety bulletin: airborne dust from blasting

text:
# SB-1005 Safety bulletin: pinch points during die change

Revision: Rev E  
Plant: P3, line P3-L3  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L3-CN02

Hazard description
Pinch points are present during die change operations on the machining and workholding assemblies of the turning center. Common pinch locations include the die clamp interface, carriage-to-saddle gap, and manual handling interfaces when aligning dies. Unexpected movement during die change can trap fingers or hands between mating components, leading to crush injuries. Contributing factors observed in recent near-miss reports include incomplete isolation of drive systems, unsecured tooling, and reliance on manual contact to guide heavy die sections into position.

Affected equipment
Primary: EQ-P3-L3-CN02 (Machining CNC turning center #2). The way lube refill interval for Machining CNC turning center #2 (EQ-P3-L3-CN02) is 70 hours. Secondary: associated die carts, hoists, and fixtures used during die change activities on line P3-L3.

Required controls
- Lockout/Tagout: Follow MM-P3-L3-CN02 for mechanical and electrical isolation before any die change activity. Ensure personal locks and verification of zero energy state prior to contact with pinch-point areas.
- Standard work: Adhere to SOP-P3-L3-01 and SOP-P3-L3-02 for stepwise die change procedures, including use of alignment tools and sequence verification. Do not bypass interlocks or sensors during procedure.
- Tooling and handling: Use approved lifting fixtures and avoid manual guiding of die edges; maintain minimum two-person lift practices when fixtures are unavailable. Keep hands clear of the die clamp interface and carriage gaps while lowering components.
- Housekeeping and maintenance: Verify way lube service is performed per schedule to maintain predictable axis motion; log service actions on the equipment history record. Inspect guards and removable covers for fastener integrity before reassembly.
- Training: Require refresher training for all personnel performing die changes on EQ-P3-L3-CN02, emphasizing hazard recognition and procedure adherence. Document competencies in the training log.

Effective date
Effective immediately. Related documents: MM-P3-L3-CN02, SOP-P3-L3-01, SOP-P3-L3-02.
title: Safety bulletin: pinch points during die change

text:
# SB-1006 — Safety bulletin: hot metal and scale ejection

Revision: Rev E  
Plant: P1, line P1-L4  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L4-HT03

Hazard description
Hot metal and scale ejection from furnace operations present impact and burn hazards to operators and bystanders, and can damage tooling, conveyors, and nearby equipment. Ejection events are most commonly observed during loading, quench entry, and quench immersion when scale fractures or molten droplets are dislodged. Contributing factors include improper containment, delayed quench entry, degraded hearth or basket condition, and failure of local shielding. The immediate risks are thermal injury, eye damage, slip hazards from quench splash, and secondary projectiles from broken scale.

Affected equipment
This bulletin applies to Heat Treat heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P1-L4-HT03) on P1-L4 and all associated quench staging and shielding fixtures used with this furnace. The quench delay maximum for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P1-L4-HT03) is 15 seconds. Related process staging areas and any manual handling stations adjacent to the furnace are included. See ECN-2026-015 for recent configuration changes, and SOP-P1-L4-03 and SOP-P1-L4-05 for operating and maintenance procedures referenced below.

Required controls
- Engineering: Verify fixed shields, splash guards, and quench entry baffles are installed per ECN-2026-015 and are free of deformation or gaps before each shift. Restrict pedestrian access to the minimum required area and install permanent signage at the exclusion boundary.  
- Administrative: Enforce adherence to SOP-P1-L4-03 and SOP-P1-L4-05 for loading, quench timing, and basket inspection. Do not exceed the specified quench delay; operators must time entry so that delay does not exceed the stated maximum. Record quench timing on the heat sheet for every cycle.  
- PPE: Require face shields, heat-resistant gloves, and arm protection for all personnel within the exclusion boundary during loading and quench operations. Provide splash mats at quench exits to mitigate slip.  
- Inspection: Implement daily visual checks of shielding and quarterly documented inspections of quench hardware; remove from service and tag out any component exhibiting cracks, excessive wear, or deformation.

Effective date
Effective date: Upon release.
title: Safety bulletin: hot metal and scale ejection

text:
# SB-1007 Safety bulletin: airborne dust from blasting

Revision: Rev B  
Plant: P2, line P2-L4  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L4-HP03

Hazard description
Blasting operations in the Heat Treat area generate airborne particulate that can penetrate local exhaust and general ventilation systems during upset conditions or when containment is compromised. Fine dust increases risk of respiratory exposure, contaminant carry into downstream machining, and accelerated wear of hydraulic system seals through ingress to adjacent spaces. The system pressure limit for Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #3 (EQ-P2-L4-HP03) is 320 bar. Loss of filtration or uncontrolled dust migration can lead to unplanned maintenance and increased safety incidents.

Affected equipment
Primary: EQ-P2-L4-HP03 (Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #3) located on line P2-L4.  
Secondary: adjacent conveyors, local extraction hoods, and portable breathing air housings in the P2 Heat Treat zone. Refer to SOP-P2-L4-01, SOP-P2-L4-02, and SOP-P2-L4-03 for routine operation and cleaning sequences that interface with blasting and press activities.

Required controls
- Containment: Maintain intact blasting curtains and negative-pressure hooding during blasting. Inspect curtain integrity before each shift; remove visible breaches and tag until repaired per SOP-P2-L4-01.  
- Ventilation: Confirm local exhaust is operating and filters are installed per manufacturer recommendations. Replace prefilters when loading is observed; do not bypass filters. See SOP-P2-L4-02 for ventilation verification steps.  
- Housekeeping: Implement immediate vacuuming with HEPA-rated units after blasting; do not use compressed air for cleaning near EQ-P2-L4-HP03. Follow cleaning checklists in SOP-P2-L4-03.  
- Isolation: When blasting occurs, isolate hydraulic access panels on EQ-P2-L4-HP03 and verify seals are engaged. Prevent dust ingress to hydraulic components and respect the system pressure limit of 320 bar during any pressure-related work.  
- PPE: Mandatory respiratory protection and eye protection for personnel within the Blast Exclusion Zone; ensure fit testing and training records are current per site requirements.  
- Monitoring: Increase airborne particulate monitoring during blasting campaigns and log results in maintenance records. Escalate excursions for corrective action.

Effective date
Rev B (effective on issuance of this bulletin)
title: Safety bulletin: airborne dust from blasting

# SB-1008: Safety bulletin: arc flash at the induction power cabinet

Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P1, line P1-L2  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L2-RR01

Hazard description
The induction power cabinet feeding the ring rolling drive has produced an arc flash event during a maintenance access sequence. The arc produced high-energy ejection of molten metal and caused electrical insulation damage inside the cabinet. There is an immediate risk of serious burn injury and secondary hazards from falling conductors and damaged control wiring. Entry into the cabinet or work on live components without established arc flash controls exposes personnel to unacceptable risk.

Affected equipment
The condition affects the induction power cabinet associated with EQ-P1-L2-RR01 and all upstream disconnects in the line P1-L2 distribution path. The maximum ring outer diameter for Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P1-L2-RR01) is 995 mm. Operators, maintenance technicians, and electricians who perform diagnostics, testing, or component replacement on this cabinet are considered potentially exposed.

Required controls
- Establish a zero-energy verification procedure and lockout/tagout before any access. Refer to SOP-P1-L2-03 for LOTO sequencing and verification steps.  
- Require arc-rated PPE and flash protection boundaries when live testing is unavoidable; consult ECN-2026-009 for approved PPE selections and cabinet repair specifications.  
- Restrict non-essential personnel from the area during troubleshooting and repairs. Document access in maintenance records and include an assigned safety observer.  
- De-energize and perform infrared and visual inspection after any arc event; follow completion steps in SOP-P1-L2-05 for post-event inspection and component replacement.  
- Suspend all ring loading and rolling operations that rely on this cabinet until repairs and verification are complete.

Effective date
Effective date: Immediate. All work on the induction power cabinet feeding EQ-P1-L2-RR01 must comply with the required controls above until engineering validation and sign-off are completed per ECN-2026-009 and SOP-P1-L2-05.
title: Safety bulletin: arc flash at the induction power cabinet
