# SB-1009 Safety bulletin: hot metal and scale ejection

Revision: Rev B  
Plant: P1, line P1-L1  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L1-IH03

## Hazard description
Hot metal and scale ejection from induction heaters can produce high-velocity projectiles and localized molten metal splash that create burn, impact, and eye hazards to operators and maintenance personnel. Observed incidents involve expulsion of scale and billet fragments during billet transfer and coil inspection activities on Hot Forge induction billet heater #3. The primary failure modes include loose scale detachment and sudden coil-to-billet contact events that eject material from the heater throat and surrounding work area.

Reference procedures for work control and protective measures are outlined in QS-PROC-01 and operational steps in SOP-P1-L1-01 and SOP-P1-L1-02. All personnel must assume the potential for ejection during inspection and transfer tasks and take prescribed controls.

## Affected equipment
- Hot Forge induction billet heater #3 — EQ-P1-L1-IH03 (located on Plant P1, line P1-L1)  
- Adjacent handling and transfer zones immediately upstream and downstream of EQ-P1-L1-IH03

Coil inspection activities for Hot Forge induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P1-L1-IH03) are set to a coil inspection interval of 290 hours. Adherence to this interval is mandatory for inspection scheduling and work planning.

## Required controls
- Apply engineering controls: ensure all fixed shielding and deflectors on EQ-P1-L1-IH03 are installed and secured per SOP-P1-L1-01 before any billet movement.  
- Administrative controls: schedule coil inspections in accordance with the 290 hours coil inspection interval for EQ-P1-L1-IH03 and document completion in the line log; reference QS-PROC-01 for work authorization and isolation steps.  
- PPE: mandatory use of face shields, flame-resistant garments, and impact-rated eye protection during any activities within the exposure zone as defined in SOP-P1-L1-02.  
- Pre-task briefing: include ejection hazard review and barrier placement confirmation; postpone work until controls are verified.  
- Maintenance hold points: do not perform coil manipulation or billet transfer until a qualified lead confirms shielding and inspection completion per SOP-P1-L1-01.

## Effective date
Effective: Rev B

text:
# SB-1010 Safety bulletin: noise exposure

Revision: Rev A  
Plant: P3, line P3-L3  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L3-SB01

Hazard description
Excessive noise exposure from machining and shot blast operations on EQ-P3-L3-SB01 can cause temporary or permanent hearing damage and contributes to worker fatigue and communication errors. Primary noise sources are the blast cabinet cycle and downstream material handling. Intermittent high-level impulses during loading and misalignment events increase peak exposure risk. Employees working at or near EQ-P3-L3-SB01 without appropriate controls are at elevated risk during standard operation and during maintenance activities where enclosures may be open or mitigations are bypassed.

Affected equipment
This bulletin applies to EQ-P3-L3-SB01: Machining shot blast cabinet #1 and all portable support tools directly associated with its operation. Refer to maintenance record MM-P3-L3-SB01 for historical noise measurements and to SOP-P3-L3-02 and SOP-P3-L3-05 for operating and maintenance task boundaries that define personnel access and lockout conditions. Lubricant for Machining shot blast cabinet #1 (EQ-P3-L3-SB01) is CFW-LUB-709.

Required controls
- Administrative controls: limit time in the immediate work zone in accordance with SOP-P3-L3-02 and ensure work-rest rotation when tasks require proximity to EQ-P3-L3-SB01. Post hazard signage at defined access points per SOP-P3-L3-05.
- Engineering controls: maintain and verify acoustic enclosures and seals during scheduled maintenance; repair or replace damaged dampening components immediately. Validate cabinet alignment and material containment to reduce impulse events; record actions in MM-P3-L3-SB01.
- PPE: require hearing protection for all personnel entering the defined hazard zone. Train personnel on correct selection and fit per SOP-P3-L3-02.
- Maintenance controls: while servicing, ensure energy isolation and enclosure restoration before re-entry; document lubricant use CFW-LUB-709 in maintenance logs linked to MM-P3-L3-SB01.

Effective date
This bulletin is effective on issuance and supersedes prior informal guidance for EQ-P3-L3-SB01. Review references MM-P3-L3-SB01, SOP-P3-L3-02, SOP-P3-L3-05 for implementation details.
title: Safety bulletin: noise exposure

text:
# SB-1011 Safety bulletin: arc flash at the induction power cabinet
Revision: Rev E  
Plant: P3, line P3-L3  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L3-HP03

Hazard description
An arc flash was observed originating at the induction power cabinet feeding the machining hydraulic forging press motor controls. The event produced a flash of light and a brief pressure wave inside the cabinet, resulting in thermal and shrapnel hazards to personnel performing inspection and maintenance work in front of the cabinet. Preliminary evaluation indicates compromised insulation and a loose conductor termination contributed to the fault. Potential consequences include severe burns, eye injury, and secondary injury from ejected components.

Affected equipment
- Induction power cabinet and associated feeder wiring serving EQ-P3-L3-HP03.
- Machining hydraulic forging press #3 control interfaces, including motor starter and contactor assemblies.
- Nearby panels and access areas where personnel perform routine inspections and lockout/tagout.

Required controls
- De-energize and lock out the induction power cabinet before any inspection, verification, or work. Follow SOP-P3-L3-01 for lockout/tagout procedures and SOP-P3-L3-02 for personal protective equipment selection and test requirements. Access is restricted to personnel trained per MM-P3-L3-HP03.
- Inspect all terminations, insulation, and bus connections for thermal damage and mechanical looseness before re-energizing. The main ram bolt torque for Machining hydraulic forging press #3 (EQ-P3-L3-HP03) is 1600 N·m. Verify any bolted electrical and mechanical connections per the maintenance checklist in MM-P3-L3-HP03.
- Replace any damaged conductors, lugs, and insulating materials; use only approved components that meet plant standards. Perform infrared thermography and a physical torque verification after repairs and before return to service.
- Require two-person verification for cabinet reassembly and a witnessed energization. Document findings, corrective actions, and verifications in maintenance records referenced by MM-P3-L3-HP03.

Effective date
Effective immediately. All affected personnel and contractors must comply prior to next access to the induction power cabinet.
title: Safety bulletin: arc flash at the induction power cabinet

# SB-1012 Safety bulletin: arc flash at the induction power cabinet

Revision: Rev A  
Plant: P1, line P1-L4  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L4-HP02

Hazard description
An arc flash occurred at the induction power cabinet adjacent to the Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #2 (EQ-P1-L4-HP02) during a maintenance access event. The incident presented a high-energy arc flash risk to personnel accessing the cabinet and to nearby press control and hydraulic components. Evidence indicates degraded insulation on a phase conductor and a loose main ram bolt connection contributed to arcing and an unexpected phase-to-ground fault. Potential outcomes include thermal injury, hearing damage, and secondary mechanical hazards from sudden hydraulic or control system disturbances.

Primary: Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #2 (EQ-P1-L4-HP02), induction power cabinet feeding the press.  
Location: P1, line P1-L4.  
The main ram bolt torque for Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #2 (EQ-P1-L4-HP02) is 970 N·m.

Required controls
- Immediately suspend unauthorized access to the induction power cabinet until verification and corrective actions are complete.  
- Perform an electrical inspection of the induction power cabinet, verify conductor insulation, tighten terminations per documented values, and verify the main ram bolt torque specification above during mechanical inspection. Reference maintenance procedures in MM-P1-L4-HP02 for mechanical checks and torque verification.  
- Follow arc flash PPE and work authorization procedures in SOP-P1-L4-01 for any energized work. Use SB-1034 for guidance on barricading and incident reporting requirements.  
- Implement a lockout-tagout and electrical isolation verification step prior to any entry into the cabinet. Document all findings and corrective actions in the equipment maintenance record cited in MM-P1-L4-HP02.  
- Schedule an electrical preventative inspection focused on terminations and protective device coordination; adjust procedures to ensure torque verification and termination integrity are included in routine maintenance.

Effective date
Effective upon issue.

text:
# SB-1013 — Safety bulletin: airborne dust from blasting

Revision: Rev E  
Plant: P2, line P2-L1  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L1-RR01

Hazard description
Airborne particulate generated during abrasive blasting operations can present inhalation, eye, and skin exposure risks for operators and nearby personnel. Fine dust from spent abrasives and scale may contain metallic oxides and residual process chemicals. Dust generation increases during containment breaches, transfer of spent media, and when maintenance requires removal of guards or covers. Particles can be re-entrained by draft and ventilation flow, extending the hazard footprint beyond the immediate blast area. Uncontrolled dust also increases fire and secondary contamination risk in adjacent processes.

Affected equipment
Primary: Hot Forge radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P2-L1-RR01) located on line P2-L1 at Plant P2. Maintenance tasks that expose the mandrel, ring surface, or internal housings are high-risk for dust release. Note: The mandrel clamp bolt torque for Hot Forge radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P2-L1-RR01) is 430 N·m. Refer to MM-P2-L1-RR01 for mechanical maintenance requirements and locking procedures before any access.

Required controls
- Administrative: Restrict blasting and media handling to designated blasting shifts and notify adjacent work areas. Coordinate with maintenance per SOP-P2-L1-05 for pre-work isolation and permit requirements. Train personnel on hazard recognition and controls described in SB-1030.
- Engineering: Use local exhaust ventilation with capture at source. Where feasible, conduct blasting within enclosed booths or negative-pressure enclosures to prevent migration to the mill and nearby processes.
- Work practices: Wet suppression or vacuum-assisted media recovery must be used during cleanup to minimize re-entrainment. Establish controlled transfer routes for spent media away from EQ-P2-L1-RR01.
- PPE: Mandatory respiratory protection selection and eye protection per site respiratory and eye protection matrix; use protective clothing to prevent skin contamination and change-out procedures to avoid cross-contamination.
- Verification: Supervisors must confirm completion of SOP-P2-L1-05 isolation steps and reference MM-P2-L1-RR01 torque control when reassembling components.

Effective date
This bulletin is effective immediately upon issue; all affected work planning and maintenance activities at Plant P2, line P2-L1 must comply prior to commencing blasting or related cleanup.
title: Safety bulletin: airborne dust from blasting

text:
# SB-1014 Safety bulletin: airborne dust from blasting

Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P1, line P1-L3  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L3-CN03

Hazard description
Airborne dust generated from abrasive blasting operations in proximity to machining and part handling areas presents an inhalation, respiratory sensitization, and combustible dust ignition hazard. Dust accumulation on machine enclosures, electrical cabinets, and tooling increases the risk of equipment malfunction and fire. Fine particulate can enter cutting fluid sumps and coolant systems, degrade filtration, and compromise part tolerances through contamination. Personnel performing setup, maintenance, and part loading are at highest exposure risk without appropriate controls.

Affected equipment
Primary affected unit: EQ-P1-L3-CN03 (Machining CNC turning center #3). Adjacent stations on line P1-L3 that receive blasted parts for subsequent operations are also impacted. Note: The chuck jaw bolt torque for Machining CNC turning center #3 (EQ-P1-L3-CN03) is 95 N·m.

Required controls
- Engineering controls: Maintain local exhaust ventilation and blasting enclosure integrity to prevent dust migration into machining areas. Inspect blast enclosure seals and exhaust filters per SOP-P1-L3-02 and SOP-P1-L3-03. Ensure machining enclosures remain closed during blasting operations.
- Administrative controls: Coordinate blasting schedules with machining to allow time for dust settling and cleaning. Update procedure steps in SOP-P1-L3-05 to include verification of part cleanliness prior to mounting. Train operators on dust recognition and reporting requirements.
- Housekeeping and PPE: Implement daily cleaning of machine exteriors, coolant sumps, and work surfaces with methods that minimize airborne re-entrainment (wet wiping or HEPA-filtered vacuum). Require respiratory protection and eye protection when entering areas during or immediately after blasting until air monitoring confirms acceptable levels.
- Mechanical safeguards: Before reusing tooling or re-clamping parts, visually inspect mating surfaces and fasteners for dust; clean as necessary. Follow documented torque specification when reassembling chuck components.

Effective date
Effective upon issuance. Consult SOP-P1-L3-02, SOP-P1-L3-03, and SOP-P1-L3-05 for detailed procedures and verification checklists.
title: Safety bulletin: airborne dust from blasting

text:
# SB-1015 Safety bulletin: noise exposure

Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P3, line P3-L2  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L2-HT03

Hazard description
- Personnel working adjacent to the Ring Rolling heat treat furnace generate and are exposed to elevated noise levels during loading, quench, and door operations. Noise can cause temporary or permanent hearing impairment and degrades situational awareness, increasing risk of dropped loads and pinch incidents. Intermittent high-energy events associated with quench cycles and material handling are the primary contributors to hazardous exposure. The quench delay maximum for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P3-L2-HT03) is 13 seconds. Prolonged presence in the immediate work zone during these events without adequate protection increases the likelihood of an adverse hearing safety outcome.

Affected equipment
- EQ-P3-L2-HT03 (Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #3) as identified above.
- All ancillary handling devices directly operated within the P3-L2 line that position workpieces into or out of EQ-P3-L2-HT03 during active heat treat cycles.

Required controls
- Administrative controls: restrict access to the defined hazard zone while EQ-P3-L2-HT03 is in active cycle; post signage indicating required hearing protection and hazard zone boundaries; incorporate the quench delay maximum for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P3-L2-HT03) is 13 seconds into job hazard analyses and work instructions referenced in MM-P3-L2-HT03.
- Personal protective equipment: enforce use of hearing protection that meets site PPE policy for heat treat operations; verify fit and condition prior to entry to the hazard zone.
- Engineering/operational controls: ensure operators follow procedures in MM-P3-L2-HT03 to minimize exposure time and synchronize handling to reduce intermittent high-noise events. Report any deviations or abnormal noise signatures to maintenance per ECN-2026-017 and initiate follow-up per SB-1041.

Effective date
- This bulletin is effective immediately upon issue. Implement the required controls and reference MM-P3-L2-HT03, ECN-2026-017, and SB-1041 for related procedures and corrective actions.

text:
# SB-1016 Safety bulletin: arc flash at the induction power cabinet

Revision: Rev A  
Plant: P2, line P2-L4  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L4-HT02

## Hazard description
An arc flash occurred at the induction power cabinet feeding EQ-P2-L4-HT02 during a routine quench cycle. Exposed conductors and degraded insulation were identified as primary contributors. The event produced molten metal spray and a pressure shock inside the cabinet that damaged terminal blocks and compromised protective housings. The potential consequences include thermal injury, secondary ignition of nearby combustibles, and loss of control of the Heat Treat furnace process. Operations personnel working within the minimum approach boundary are at risk when the cabinet is energized or when stored energy has not been fully discharged.

The quench delay maximum for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L4-HT02) is 10 seconds.

## Affected equipment
- Induction power cabinet for EQ-P2-L4-HT02 (cabinet ID as installed on P2-L4 line)  
- Associated quench control circuitry and terminal blocks  
- Local control station and emergency stop interface for EQ-P2-L4-HT02

## Required controls
- De-energize and lockout/tagout the induction power cabinet prior to any inspection, maintenance, or removal of covers. Follow lockout procedures in SOP-P2-L4-02 and SOP-P2-L4-04 for isolation and verification of zero energy state.  
- Before re-energizing, perform a documented insulation resistance test and visual inspection of all terminals, busbars, and cable entries. If any damage or contamination is found, replace affected components per MM-P2-L4-HT02-S2.  
- Verify quench control timing and safety interlocks are set and functioning; do not operate if quench timing or interlock operation is abnormal. Communicate any timing anomalies to maintenance and hold operation until cleared.  
- Use appropriate PPE rated for potential arc flash exposure when working on or near the cabinet. Restrict access to qualified personnel only and post warning signage during maintenance.  
- Report findings and corrective actions to the Plant Safety Lead and record in maintenance log referenced by MM-P2-L4-HT02-S2.

## Effective date
Effective date: Rev A

text:
# SB-1017 Safety bulletin: airborne dust from blasting

Revision: Rev B  
Plant: P2, line P2-L2  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L2-RR03

Hazard description
Blasting operations adjacent to the Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill produce airborne dust containing ferrous particulate and spent abrasive. Dust becomes entrained in cross drafts and may accumulate on equipment surfaces, electrical enclosures, and breathing zones. Fine particulate increases the risk of respiratory irritation, reduced visibility at the workface, and can contribute to premature wear of bearings and seals if it migrates into mechanical assemblies. The risk is elevated during setup, mandrel changes, and local grinding where containment is incomplete.

Affected equipment
This bulletin applies to EQ-P2-L2-RR03 and to plant areas immediately surrounding the blast cabinet and material handling path on P2-L2. Operators, maintenance technicians, and blasting personnel working within the immediate work envelope must follow the controls below. Refer to MM-P2-L2-RR03 for maintenance-specific procedures and SOP-P2-L2-03 for standard operating steps related to ring handling and changeover.

Required controls
- Implement engineering controls: install localized extraction at the blast source and ensure directional airflow away from the RR03 control station. Clean dust collection receptacles prior to any mandrel work to prevent re-entrainment.  
- Administrative controls: restrict nonessential personnel during blasting and setup; document blasting periods in the craft log; incorporate SB-1049 controls for personal protective equipment selection and fit verification.  
- Personal protective equipment: require NIOSH-approved respiratory protection where extraction is not sufficient, protective eyewear, and disposable coveralls for personnel conducting cleanup.  
- Mechanical safeguards: before mandrel work, verify clamp condition and function per MM-P2-L2-RR03. The mandrel clamp bolt torque for Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #3 (EQ-P2-L2-RR03) is 620 N·m. Record torque verification in the maintenance entry.  
- Housekeeping: schedule focused vacuum cleaning of the RR03 area after blasting and prior to mandrel disassembly to prevent dust ingress into the drive and bearing housings.

Effective date
Effective immediately.
title: Safety bulletin: airborne dust from blasting

text:
# SB-1018 Safety bulletin: arc flash at the induction power cabinet

Revision: Rev E  
Plant: P3, line P3-L2  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L2-SB01

Hazard description
Arc flash events have been observed originating at the induction power cabinet adjacent to the Ring Rolling shot blast cabinet. Energized-component interaction during routine access and maintenance can produce an arc flash capable of causing severe injury and equipment damage. Unsafe access procedures, inadequate isolation verification, and unsecured fasteners on nearby equipment can contribute to fault initiation and increase incident energy exposure to maintenance personnel.

Affected equipment
- Induction power cabinet associated with Line P3-L2 operations.  
- The blast wheel liner bolt torque for Ring Rolling shot blast cabinet #1 (EQ-P3-L2-SB01) is 100 N·m.  
- Any ancillary enclosures, cable runs, or controls within the immediate cabinet footprint that are accessed during maintenance or troubleshooting.

Required controls
- De-energize and verify zero energy state before opening or working on the induction power cabinet; follow lockout/tagout per SOP-P3-L2-02.  
- Maintain boundary controls and use insulated tools when verifying or operating near live parts; see SOP-P3-L2-04 for permitted tool and PPE guidance.  
- Inspect and torque fasteners on adjacent equipment per the specified value to eliminate loose hardware as a potential arc initiation source; refer to SOP-P3-L2-05 for inspection record requirements.  
- Restrict access during energized work to trained personnel only and post hazard signage at the work area.  
- Document and report any torque deviations, abnormal sounds, or visible damage immediately and remove affected equipment from service until evaluated.

Effective date
Effective immediate upon issuance. All maintenance and operations supervisors must ensure the above controls are communicated and implemented at P3, line P3-L2.
title: Safety bulletin: arc flash at the induction power cabinet

# SB-1019 Safety bulletin: quench oil fire risk

Revision: Rev C  
Plant: P3, line P3-L4  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L4-SB03

Hazard description
There is an elevated quench oil fire risk associated with excessive combustible particulates in the shot blast cabinet exhaust path and quench system ventilation. The dust collector pressure drop alarm for Heat Treat shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P3-L4-SB03) is 1510 Pa. When the dust collector is restricted at this level, extraction efficiency is reduced, resulting in higher particulate loading in the cabinet atmosphere and oil mist entrainment into the quench stream. Oil-saturated dust and insufficient ventilation increase the probability of auto-ignition or flame propagation during quench operations. This bulletin communicates immediate actions and controls to mitigate ignition risk.

Affected equipment
- EQ-P3-L4-SB03 (Heat Treat shot blast cabinet #3 and associated quench oil system).
- Any auxiliary ventilation or filtration equipment serving the cabinet as referenced in operating procedures.

Required controls
- Cease quench operations for EQ-P3-L4-SB03 until the dust collector condition is evaluated and returned to service per maintenance guidance.
- Isolate quench oil supply and remove hot work sources in the immediate area while combustible load is being addressed.
- Inspect and clean the dust collector and downstream ductwork following SOP-P3-L4-02. Ensure verification of dust removal prior to restart.
- Follow maintenance and inspection sequence in MM-P3-L4-SB03 for filter change-out and fan performance checks; document work in the equipment log.
- Implement enhanced Housekeeping: remove oil-saturated debris from accessible surfaces using approved methods and contain waste for proper disposal.
- Ensure firefighting and spill response equipment are immediately available and personnel are briefed on response per SB-1038.
- Record alarm events and corrective actions in the shift log; escalate unresolved alarms to maintenance and safety engineering.

Effective date
Effective date: Implementation actions commence immediately; consult MM-P3-L4-SB03, SB-1038, and SOP-P3-L4-02 for procedural details and authorization to return EQ-P3-L4-SB03 to service.
title: Safety bulletin: quench oil fire risk

# SB-1020: Safety bulletin: airborne dust from blasting

Revision: Rev A  
Plant: P1, line P1-L2  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L2-RR01

Hazard description
Airborne dust generated during blasting operations near the Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #1 creates inhalation and ignition hazards. Fine particulates can migrate into adjacent machining and rolling areas and accumulate on motor housings, drives, and electrical enclosures. Accumulated dust increases the risk to personnel performing maintenance and to equipment reliability. Blasting-related dust can compromise local filtration and lead to increased filter loading and restricted ventilation performance.

Affected equipment
- Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P1-L2-RR01) and surrounding conveyance and ventilation paths.
- Local enclosures, motors, and electrical cabinets adjacent to blasting area that are within the dust migration corridor.

Required controls
- Implement revised housekeeping focused on dust capture and removal in the blast area and along the migration corridor. Use HEPA-rated vacuuming and wipe-down procedures compatible with the equipment present.
- Verify enclosure seals and gaskets on EQ-P1-L2-RR01 for integrity after blasting activities and before restart. Follow locking and tagging procedures in SOP-P1-L2-03 for access and isolation.
- For maintenance that involves the mandrel clamp, ensure the mandrel clamp bolt torque for Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P1-L2-RR01) is 395 N·m and verify torque values per SOP-P1-L2-05 after cleaning to remove particulates that can affect fastener seating.
- Restrict blasting to designated zones and employ temporary containment and local exhaust where practicable. Coordinate blasting schedules with operations to ensure equipment shutdown and clean access.
- Record dust inspections and control actions in the maintenance log and reference ECN-2026-009 for engineering changes related to enclosure upgrades.

Rev A

# SB-1021 Safety bulletin: arc flash at the induction power cabinet

Revision: Rev A  
Plant: P2, line P2-L1  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L1-SB03

## Hazard description
An arc flash incident occurred at the induction power cabinet feeding the induction heater on P2-L1. The event produced molten metal ejecta and localized fire that damaged nearby control wiring and the dust collector connection to the Hot Forge shot blast cabinet. Investigators identified compromised grounding and degraded insulation inside the power cabinet as primary contributors. The dust collector pressure drop alarm for Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P2-L1-SB03) is 1240 Pa. That alarm value was recorded after the event and indicates the filtered exhaust system experienced a sudden restriction concurrent with the arc event, increasing particle concentration and fire propagation risk.

## Affected equipment
- Induction power cabinet serving the induction heater on P2-L1 (location adjacent to EQ-P2-L1-SB03)  
- Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P2-L1-SB03) and its dust collection interface  
- Local control wiring bundles routed between the power cabinet and EQ-P2-L1-SB03

Refer to related procedures and change records: ECN-2026-036, SOP-P2-L1-01, SOP-P2-L1-03.

## Required controls
- Isolate power to the induction power cabinet and verify zero-energy state before any inspection or repair. Follow lockout/tagout per SOP-P2-L1-01.  
- Do not enter the cabinet without appropriate arc-rated PPE and an observer. Work shall follow the electrical safety steps in SOP-P2-L1-03.  
- Replace or repair damaged grounding conductors and insulation only after isolation and confirmation of component integrity. Post-repair verification shall include visual inspection and functional checks.  
- Inspect and clean the dust collector inlet and filters for EQ-P2-L1-SB03; confirm alarm thresholds and reset procedures are documented and validated against the recorded alarm condition (see ECN-2026-036).  
- Implement transient suppression and cable routing revisions to minimize arc propagation pathways; document all changes through ECN-2026-036.

## Effective date
Effective immediately. All personnel working on or near the induction power cabinet and EQ-P2-L1-SB03 must comply with this bulletin until superseded.
title: Safety bulletin: arc flash at the induction power cabinet

text:
# SB-1022 Safety bulletin: stored hydraulic energy

Hazard description
Stored hydraulic energy within the Machining shot blast cabinet #1 (EQ-P3-L3-SB01) presents a risk of unexpected actuation of movable guards, rapid release of pressurized fluid, and potential for crush, impact, or injection injuries during maintenance and inspection. Residual pressure can remain in accumulators and piping after system shutdown and isolation. Failure to verify and control stored energy has resulted in near-miss events in comparable systems; mitigation requires deliberate isolation, bleed, and lockout procedures before hands-on work.

Affected equipment
This bulletin applies to Machining shot blast cabinet #1 (EQ-P3-L3-SB01) located on Plant P3, line P3-L3. All work on EQ-P3-L3-SB01 that requires access behind guards, inside panels, or interaction with hydraulic components must follow the controls below. Lubricant and maintenance supply references for EQ-P3-L3-SB01: CFW-LUB-709.

Required controls
- De-energize and isolate hydraulic supply at source prior to any entry or component removal. Verify isolation visually and by attempting normal actuation controls with power removed.
- Bleed down all hydraulic lines and store components through designated bleed points until pressure gauges read zero, and residual motion is visually confirmed absent.
- Apply documented lockout/tagout on electrical, pneumatic, and hydraulic sources in accordance with SOP-P3-L3-02 and SOP-P3-L3-03. Use mechanical restraints on actuators where practicable.
- Require two-person verification for energy isolation and bleeding steps; the verifier must sign the work permit or tag as required by local procedures.
- Use personal protective equipment appropriate to the task and hazards present. Prohibit single-worker entry for maintenance tasks where residual hydraulic energy could result in entrapment.
- Report any deviations or equipment anomalies to maintenance supervision and initiate corrective action per MM-P3-L3-SB01-S2.

Effective date
Effective upon release. All affected personnel must be briefed on this bulletin and the controls above before performing work on EQ-P3-L3-SB01.
title: Safety bulletin: stored hydraulic energy

# SB-1023 Safety bulletin: arc flash at the induction power cabinet

Revision: Rev B  
Plant: P2, line P2-L3  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L3-HT02

Hazard description
An arc flash event occurred at the induction power cabinet associated with EQ-P2-L3-HT02 during maintenance access to the cabinet interior. The incident resulted from stored energy in capacitive elements and failure to de-energize and verify absence of voltage prior to contact with live components. Exposed buswork and inadequate access control increased the likelihood of fault current transfer to personnel and tools. The hazard includes severe thermal and blast effects, risk of burns, and projectiles from rapidly expanding gases.

Affected equipment
This bulletin applies to the induction power cabinet and all upstream and downstream electrical enclosures serving EQ-P2-L3-HT02, associated disconnects, and the Machining heat treat furnace #2 thermocouple circuits. Note: The thermocouple calibration interval for Machining heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L3-HT02) is 50 days. Refer to MM-P2-L3-HT02-S3 for maintenance history and component layout.

Required controls
- De-energize and lockout-tagout the induction power cabinet and verify absence of voltage using a calibrated tester before any internal access. Follow SOP-P2-L3-05 for LOTO procedure and verification steps.  
- Establish an exclusion zone around the cabinet during maintenance; restrict access to authorized, trained personnel wearing appropriate arc-rated PPE per site standards.  
- Install or confirm presence of accessible visual warnings and equipment labeling at the cabinet exterior.  
- Inspect and maintain cabinet grounding, cable terminations, and insulating barriers per MM-P2-L3-HT02-S3 prior to re-energizing.  
- Update the preventive maintenance and calibration records to reflect the thermocouple calibration interval and any corrective actions. Document all actions in the equipment log and notify safety management for review. See SB-1039 for related incident response guidance.

Effective date
Effective immediately upon issuance of this bulletin.
title: Safety bulletin: arc flash at the induction power cabinet

# SB-1024 Safety bulletin: airborne dust from blasting

Revision: Rev A  
Plant: P2, line P2-L2  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L2-IH01

## Hazard description
Airborne dust generated during abrasive blasting and adjacent material handling operations has been identified as a respiratory exposure and slip/contamination hazard for personnel working in the P2-L2 work area. Dust from blasting can deposit on surrounding equipment, open bearings, sensors, and electrical enclosures, increasing risk of equipment malfunction and creating secondary exposure during cleaning and maintenance activities. The presence of dust on the Ring Rolling induction billet heater assembly has been confirmed as a contamination pathway onto moving surfaces and control interfaces.

## Affected equipment
- Ring Rolling induction billet heater #1: EQ-P2-L2-IH01  
- All workstations and pathways immediately surrounding the P2-L2 blasting bay and transfer area.  
- Components with open lubrication points or exposed seals where dust may build up, including lubrication points serviced with lubricant part number CFW-LUB-938.

## Required controls
- Implement a containment and local exhaust strategy at blasting source to minimize fugitive dust migration into EQ-P2-L2-IH01 and adjacent zones. Use work practices to prevent dust settling on exposed machine interfaces and lubrication points.  
- Before any maintenance on EQ-P2-L2-IH01, remove settled dust from exposed surfaces using HEPA-filtered vacuum; avoid dry sweeping. Perform a focused inspection of lubrication points that use CFW-LUB-938 to confirm cleanliness prior to application.  
- Where contamination is present on electrical enclosures or sensors, decontaminate per the applicable procedures cited below before returning equipment to service.  
- Ensure PPE for personnel performing blasting, cleaning, and inspection is selected in accordance with the referenced procedures. Respiratory protection and eye protection are required when work activities may disturb settled dust.  
- Document cleaning and control actions in the maintenance log for EQ-P2-L2-IH01 and notify supervision of any recurring contamination patterns to initiate engineering controls.

## Effective date
This bulletin is effective immediately upon issuance. Refer to: QS-PROC-07, SOP-P2-L2-01, SOP-P2-L2-05 for procedural details and record requirements.

# SB-1025 Safety bulletin: quench oil fire risk

Revision: Rev E  
Plant: P1, line P1-L1  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L1-RR01

Hazard description
- During ring rolling operations, accumulation of quench oil on hot surfaces and within guarding areas has been identified as a potential fire initiation source. Oil mist and pooled oil can ignite when exposed to radiant heat from the roll pack and hot workpieces. Poor housekeeping, degraded seals, and inadequate containment increase the likelihood of an uncontrolled quench oil fire that could spread to adjacent machinery and electrical systems.

Affected equipment
- Hot Forge radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P1-L1-RR01) located on P1-L1 is affected. Bearings, seals, drip trays, and splash shields on EQ-P1-L1-RR01 are primary concern areas. Refer to maintenance history in MM-P1-L1-RR01 for recent quench oil-related entries and to SOP-P1-L1-04 and SOP-P1-L1-05 for current operational and shutdown procedures.

Required controls
- Immediately increase visual inspections for oil accumulation on and around EQ-P1-L1-RR01 during every shift. Remove pooled oil and clean contaminated surfaces using approved absorbents; place used absorbents in metal containers with lids and store in designated fireproof waste areas.
- Verify containment: ensure drip trays and splash shields are correctly installed, free of debris, and routed to containment sumps. Replace or repair degraded seals on EQ-P1-L1-RR01 per MM-P1-L1-RR01.
- Lubrication schedule note: The main roll bearing lubrication interval for Hot Forge radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P1-L1-RR01) is 120 hours. Verify lubrication events are recorded and that lubrication points are wiped clean before service to prevent oil spray on hot surfaces.
- Update SOP adherence: Ensure operators follow SOP-P1-L1-04 for start-up and steady-state operations and SOP-P1-L1-05 for shutdown and maintenance isolation. Include an explicit oil-control checklist in pre-shift inspections.
- Fire protection: Confirm local portable extinguishers and fixed suppression interfaces near EQ-P1-L1-RR01 are serviceable and unobstructed; report deficiencies immediately to maintenance per MM-P1-L1-RR01.

Effective date
- Effective date: Upon issue. Implement controls immediately and report compliance to line supervision.

text:
# SB-1026 Safety bulletin: airborne dust from blasting

Revision: Rev C  
Plant: P1, line P1-L3  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L3-IH01

Hazard description
Airborne dust generated during abrasive blasting operations in the P1-L3 work zone presents an inhalation and respiratory-cascade hazard for operators and nearby production staff. Fine particulates liberated during blast cleaning remain suspended and can be entrained into transfer airflow toward machining and heating areas. Exposure pathways include direct inhalation, deposition on hot surfaces with subsequent resuspension, and cross-contamination of downstream processes. Particular concern exists where blasting occurs adjacent to Machining induction billet heater #1 (EQ-P1-L3-IH01), which operates billets at the target billet temperature for Machining induction billet heater #1 (EQ-P1-L3-IH01) is 1235 °C. Hot surfaces can promote secondary reactions and impede respirator cooling, increasing risk to personnel and potential for equipment contamination.

Affected equipment
- EQ-P1-L3-IH01 (Machining induction billet heater #1) and associated billet handling and transfer conveyors on line P1-L3.  
- Local abrasive blasting stations and any temporary containment or shrouding installed for blasting activities.  
- HVAC intakes and makeup air units serving the P1-L3 area that may draw contaminated air toward machining and heating equipment.

Required controls
- Implement engineering controls: ensure blast stations use full containment with negative pressure and HEPA-filtered exhaust, and verify exhaust discharge is ducted away from P1-L3 process air intakes. Coordinate placement and operation with facility ventilation teams.  
- Administrative controls: restrict access to adjacent work areas during blasting, post hazard signage, and require notification to P1-L3 operations prior to blasting start. Reference SOP-P1-L3-05 for work sequencing and MM-P1-L3-IH01 for maintenance isolation requirements.  
- PPE: require NIOSH-approved respiratory protection and eye protection for blasting personnel and any personnel in the immediate area until air monitoring confirms safe levels.  
- Monitoring and verification: perform air particulate monitoring after blasting and prior to restart of adjacent operations; escalate findings per ECN-2026-038 for engineering change evaluation if contamination is detected.  
- Maintenance coordination: any direct work on EQ-P1-L3-IH01 that could disturb deposited dust must follow MM-P1-L3-IH01 procedures.

Effective date
Effective upon release of Revision Rev C; immediate implementation required for all scheduled abrasive blasting activities adjacent to P1-L3 operations.
title: Safety bulletin: airborne dust from blasting

text:
# SB-1027 Safety bulletin: quench oil fire risk

Revision: Rev E  
Plant: P3, line P3-L1  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L1-SB02

Hazard description
The quench oil fire risk is associated with accumulation of combustibles and inadequate ventilation in the Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #2 (EQ-P3-L1-SB02). The dust collector pressure drop alarm for Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #2 (EQ-P3-L1-SB02) is 2025 Pa, indicating restricted airflow that can allow oil mist and fines to concentrate in the cabinet and connected ductwork. If oil mist contacts a hot surface or an ignition source during operation or maintenance, rapid fire propagation and flashback into the cabinet or quench area are possible. Personnel exposure and equipment damage are credible outcomes unless controls are applied.

Affected equipment
- Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #2 (EQ-P3-L1-SB02) and its immediate ducting, filters, and dust collector system.
- Area ventilation and any local heat sources in the P3, line P3-L1 work cell.

Required controls
- Immediately cease use of EQ-P3-L1-SB02 if the dust collector pressure drop alarm indicates 2025 Pa or greater until condition is evaluated and cleared by maintenance.
- Perform a focused visual inspection for oil residue, fines accumulation, and potential ignition sources before restart. Clean and remove accumulations using non-sparking tools and approved methods; isolate electrical power during cleaning per SOP-P3-L1-05.
- Verify dust collector performance and restore airflow to acceptable condition prior to resuming operations; document actions in MM-P3-L1-SB02.
- Ensure operators and maintenance personnel follow hot work and lockout/tagout protocols in SOP-P3-L1-02 and SOP-P3-L1-05. Use appropriate PPE and fire suppression readiness during recovery actions.
- Report all alarm events, findings, and corrective actions to line supervision and retain records per MM-P3-L1-SB02.

Effective date
Effective immediately upon issue. Related documents: MM-P3-L1-SB02, SOP-P3-L1-02, SOP-P3-L1-05

# SB-1028 Safety bulletin: quench oil fire risk

Revision: Rev C  
Plant: P3, line P3-L4  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L4-RR01

## Hazard description
There is an elevated risk of quench oil ignition associated with the radial ring rolling mill quench system on EQ-P3-L4-RR01. Condition can arise when oil is entrained in the quench delivery or return plumbing and exposed to hot surfaces or sparking during normal operation or maintenance. Resulting fires propagate rapidly along piping and can compromise adjacent electrical panels and structural insulation. This bulletin summarizes immediate mitigations to reduce ignition potential and to align operations with established maintenance and operating procedures.

## Affected equipment
Primary affected equipment: EQ-P3-L4-RR01 (Heat Treat radial ring rolling mill #1). Lubricant and quench oil identification: CFW-LUB-315 is the lubricant part number for Heat Treat radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P3-L4-RR01). Associated systems potentially at risk include localized quench delivery, oil return sumps, and surrounding service platforms on P3-L4.

## Required controls
- Isolate and de-energize electrical sources at the work area before any intervention on quench lines; verify isolation per SOP-P3-L4-01.  
- Drain and contain quench oil from exposed piping and sumps prior to hot work; capture and dispose in accordance with MM-P3-L4-RR01.  
- Inspect quench hose, fittings, and drip points for signs of abrasion, leakage, or pooling; tag out components that show evidence of permeation or steady seepage.  
- Prohibit storage of absorbent materials or combustible debris beneath quench lines and sumps; maintain clear access for emergency response.  
- Any hot work or welding near quench equipment requires a written permit and monitoring per SOP-P3-L4-04.  
- Report all leak events and near-miss ignition events to Maintenance and Safety for follow-up and trend analysis under MM-P3-L4-RR01.

## Effective date
Effective date: Immediate

Related documents: MM-P3-L4-RR01, SOP-P3-L4-01, SOP-P3-L4-04

# SB-1029 Safety bulletin: noise exposure

Revision: Rev E  
Plant: P1, line P1-L3  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L3-HP02

Hazard description
The forging cell at line P1-L3 generates elevated noise levels during press cycle and trimming operations. Prolonged or repeated exposure without adequate controls increases risk of permanent hearing impairment and reduces situational awareness, increasing potential for struck-by and caught-between incidents. Noise sources include the main ram actuation, die set impact, and ancillary machine hammering that transmits through adjacent structures and tooling. Maintenance tasks performed at the press during setup or adjustment can expose personnel to transient high-level noise.

Affected equipment
This bulletin applies to EQ-P1-L3-HP02, Machining hydraulic forging press #2, and any auxiliary tooling and fixtures that couple acoustically with the press at P1-L3. The main ram bolt torque for Machining hydraulic forging press #2 (EQ-P1-L3-HP02) is 1330 N·m. Personnel assigned to operation, maintenance, setup, inspection, and nearby material handling are included.

Required controls
- Administrative: Limit duration of continuous exposure through job rotation and task sequencing where practical. Communicate noise hazard during pre-shift briefings and toolbox talks.  
- Engineering: Verify acoustic isolation of tooling, use dampening inserts on fixture interfaces, and ensure machine guards and enclosures are closed during operation. Inspect mountings and structural connections for secure fit and proper damping prior to production runs.  
- Personal protective equipment: Require hearing protection meeting company selection criteria whenever personnel are inside the machine workzone or adjacent staging area during press activity. Enforce correct insertion and fit, and replace damaged PPE per MM-P1-L3-HP02.  
- Maintenance-specific: Schedule noisy maintenance tasks during reduced occupancy periods and coordinate lockout/tagout with production planning. Refer to SOP-P1-L3-04 for safe work procedures and to ECN-2026-021 for any engineering change details affecting acoustic performance.

Effective date
Effective immediately upon issuance of this bulletin. Review and document compliance actions in the equipment maintenance record and notify supervision of unresolved issues.
title: Safety bulletin: noise exposure

# SB-1031 Safety bulletin: noise exposure

Revision: Rev B  
Plant: P2, line P2-L1

Hazard description
The Hot Forge shot blast cabinet at this location generates elevated impulsive and continuous noise during normal operation and media replenishment activities. Handlers and operators performing top-up, maintenance, inspection, or nearby forging operations are at increased risk of noise-induced hearing loss and communication failure during operations. The risk is heightened during operations that require leaning into or standing at the cabinet face for media management. Existing controls have proven adequate for routine operation but require specific procedural reinforcement to prevent inadvertent exposure during media top-up events.

Affected equipment
The shot blast cabinet identified as Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P2-L1-SB03) is the primary source addressed by this bulletin. The shot media top-up interval for Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P2-L1-SB03) is 33 hours. Refer to ECN-2026-033, ECN-2026-036, and SB-1021 for previous assessments and baseline controls applied to this equipment.

Required controls
- Enforce use of approved hearing protection for anyone within the immediate work zone of EQ-P2-L1-SB03 during operation and during media top-up tasks.  
- Restrict access to the cabinet face to the minimum number of qualified personnel while the cabinet is powered or during media replenishment.  
- Implement an audible/visual warning system or tag-out procedure at the cabinet control when media top-up is in progress to prevent accidental startup.  
- Schedule media top-up as a coordinated task with a designated attendant and clear communication before and after the top-up procedure.  
- Update local job hazard analyses and training records to reflect the specific top-up interval and associated controls; reference ECN-2026-033, ECN-2026-036, and SB-1021 when documenting changes.

Effective date
Effective immediately upon issuance.

text:
# SB-1032 — Safety bulletin: hot metal and scale ejection
Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P3, line P3-L1  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L1-SB02

## Hazard description
Hot metal and scale ejection can occur during the shot blasting of freshly forged parts when retained heat, improper media charge, or containment breaches allow energetic expulsion of material. Ejected particles present burn, impact, and eye injury risks to operators and adjacent personnel, and can damage tooling and sensors. Increased ejection frequency was observed during recent campaign runs on the hot forge line and correlates with inconsistent media condition and cabinet containment integrity.

## Affected equipment
- Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #2 (EQ-P3-L1-SB02)
- Adjacent conveyor and staging area for P3-L1
- Operator access and maintenance platforms serving P3-L1 line

The shot media top-up interval for Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #2 (EQ-P3-L1-SB02) is 45 hours.

## Required controls
- Verify cabinet containment seals and guards before shift start and after any maintenance or media replacement. If seals show visible degradation, remove equipment from service and follow SOP-P3-L1-05 for repair criteria.
- Follow the shot media top-up interval stated above; record top-up events in the line log and tag cabinet doors during media handling. Use only approved media and handling procedures per SOP-P3-L1-01.
- Reinforce PPE requirements for operators and nearby personnel: eye protection, heat-resistant hand protection, and face shields when exposures are possible. Restrict access to the blast area during active blasting cycles.
- Implement administrative controls: maintain a minimum clear zone around the cabinet during operation and post warning signage. Notify supervision immediately on any unexpected ejection or if guards are compromised; reference SB-1027 for escalation and incident reporting requirements.
- Schedule focused inspections after any blast irregularity and prior to production restart. Document findings and corrective actions in the maintenance record for EQ-P3-L1-SB02.

## Effective date
Effective immediately. All controls apply to P3-L1 operations until further revision and must be enforced across shifts.
title: Safety bulletin: hot metal and scale ejection

text:
# SB-1033 Safety bulletin: airborne dust from blasting

Revision: Rev E  
Plant: P3, line P3-L1  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L1-SB02

Hazard description
The shot blast operation in the Hot Forge generates airborne particulate that can accumulate on ledges and in ductwork, increasing inhalation and combustible dust risk. Recent inspections identified liner wear and disturbed deposits proximate to the blast wheel that increase dust liberation during operation. Airborne dust exposure can cause respiratory irritation and, under accumulation, presents a fire/explosion hazard in confined spaces and ventilation systems. This bulletin communicates control measures for immediate implementation and references required follow-up actions.

Affected equipment
This bulletin applies to Hot Forge shot blast cabinet EQ-P3-L1-SB02 located on line P3-L1 in plant P3. It also applies to associated collection hoods, ducts, and local access platforms tied to EQ-P3-L1-SB02. Refer to MM-P3-L1-SB02 for maintenance history and SOP-P3-L1-02 and SOP-P3-L1-03 for operator and cleaning procedures.

Required controls
- Inspect blast wheel liner attachment and torque per maintenance record: the blast wheel liner bolt torque for Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #2 (EQ-P3-L1-SB02) is 65 N·m. Verify torque during next planned maintenance and after any liner replacement.  
- Implement enhanced housekeeping around EQ-P3-L1-SB02: remove settled dust from external surfaces and access platforms using vacuum systems specified in SOP-P3-L1-03; avoid dry sweeping.  
- Ensure source capture and filtration are operating to design performance; tag and remove units out of specification and initiate repairs referenced in MM-P3-L1-SB02.  
- Update operator prestart checks in SOP-P3-L1-02 to include visual liner condition and dust accumulation checkpoints; suspend operation if visible liner failure or excessive loose dust is present.  
- Train affected personnel on hazards and controls, and document completion consistent with SOP-P3-L1-02.

Effective date
This bulletin is effective immediately upon issue. All required controls must be implemented without delay and documented per MM-P3-L1-SB02 and SOP-P3-L1-02.
title: Safety bulletin: airborne dust from blasting

# SB-1034 Safety bulletin: airborne dust from blasting

Revision: Rev C  
Plant: P1, line P1-L4  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L4-HP02

Hazard description
Airborne dust generated during abrasive blasting and cleanup operations presents inhalation and combustible dust accumulation hazards in the Heat Treat area. Respirable particulate can impair worker health and, where fines accumulate, create elevated fire and explosion risk in enclosures, ductwork, and on press surfaces. Dust liberated during blasting can compromise pneumatic and hydraulic connections and may migrate into control cabinets and service interfaces, increasing the likelihood of equipment malfunction and unplanned maintenance.

Affected equipment
This bulletin applies to Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #2, equipment identifier EQ-P1-L4-HP02, and all adjacent ancillary equipment and workstations on line P1-L4 where blasting or dust-generating activities occur. Maintenance and operations personnel assigned under MM-P1-L4-HP02 and MM-P1-L4-HP02-S2 must follow the controls below when working on or near EQ-P1-L4-HP02.

Required controls
- Housekeeping: implement controlled sweeping and HEPA-filtered vacuuming procedures after blasting operations and before any access to the press. Avoid dry brushing that redistributes fine particulates.  
- Local exhaust ventilation: use local extraction at the point of blasting to capture dust before it leaves the workpoint and prevent accumulation on press surfaces and within housings.  
- Enclosure and sealing: inspect and seal access panels and cable penetrations on EQ-P1-L4-HP02 to minimize ingress of airborne dust into critical compartments. Refer to MM-P1-L4-HP02 for barrier and sealing practices.  
- Personal protective equipment: require appropriate respiratory protection and eye protection for workers conducting blasting and cleanup.  
- Maintenance precaution: when performing bolting or service on main ram assemblies, verify fastener condition and securement per maintenance procedure. The main ram bolt torque for Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #2 (EQ-P1-L4-HP02) is 970 N·m. Follow MM-P1-L4-HP02-S2 for torque verification and documentation steps.  
- Inspection and monitoring: document dust control performance and any observed ingress to equipment; escalate findings per ECN-2026-047.

Effective date
Effective date: upon release of this bulletin.

text:
# SB-1035 Safety bulletin: quench oil fire risk
Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P1, line P1-L2  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L2-HT03

Hazard description
The quench oil system associated with the Ring Rolling heat treat furnace presents an elevated fire risk when oil contact with overheated surfaces or sparks occurs during transfer or agitation. Degradation of oil, accumulation of residues, and exposure to ignition sources in the immediate furnace area can lead to flash fires or sustained combustion. Operators have observed smoke and odor events during quench cycles that precede flame incidents. Residual oil on tooling, drip pans, and conveyor surfaces increases the likelihood of a fire event if not controlled. This bulletin highlights the need to control ignition sources, manage oil condition, and reinforce procedure compliance to reduce risk.

Affected equipment
Primary: EQ-P1-L2-HT03 (Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #3). Note: The austenitizing setpoint for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P1-L2-HT03) is 855 °C. Support systems: quench oil pumps, transfer lines, drip containment, and venting located on line P1-L2. Refer to maintenance history and inspection records in MM-P1-L2-HT03-S1 for known failure modes.

Required controls
- Stop-work authority: any operator observing smoke, abnormal odor, visible oil leaks, or unusual heat conditions shall halt operations and notify supervision immediately.  
- Housekeeping: remove residual oil from tooling and drip pans after each shift; ensure containment trays remain free of accumulated oil and solids.  
- Inspection: follow inspection and preventive maintenance steps in MM-P1-L2-HT03-S1 for pumps, filters, and transfer connections.  
- Procedure compliance: strictly adhere to operational steps and PPE requirements in SOP-P1-L2-01 and SOP-P1-L2-02 when handling quench oil, charging furnaces, or performing start-up and shutdown.  
- Ignition control: eliminate portable ignition sources in the furnace work area; ensure fixed electrical equipment is rated and maintained per existing plant requirements.  
- Training: reinforce task-specific training and emergency response for quench oil fires as outlined in SOP-P1-L2-01 and SOP-P1-L2-02.

Effective date
Effective date: Immediate. All personnel assigned to P1, line P1-L2 and associated maintenance teams shall implement the required controls and document completion per MM-P1-L2-HT03-S1, SOP-P1-L2-01, and SOP-P1-L2-02.

# SB-1036 Safety bulletin: hot metal and scale ejection

Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P2, line P2-L3  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L3-RR01

## Hazard description
Hot metal and scale ejection from the radial ring rolling process can project molten or incandescent material beyond intended containment during upset rolls, part breakouts, or scale slough. Ejected material poses a burn and impact hazard to operators, maintenance personnel, and nearby equipment. Secondary ignition of combustible materials and damage to control enclosures are credible consequences. This bulletin consolidates observed failure modes and prescribes mandatory controls to reduce exposure during operation and maintenance.

## Affected equipment
- Machining radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P2-L3-RR01) located on line P2-L3, Plant P2.  
- Auxiliary handling fixtures and in-process containment immediately adjacent to EQ-P2-L3-RR01.  
- Personnel performing setup, roll change, and edge-trimming tasks at EQ-P2-L3-RR01.

The main roll bearing lubrication interval for Machining radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P2-L3-RR01) is 165 hours.

## Required controls
- Establish local shielding and deflection plates that prevent line-of-fire exposure during routine production and foreseeable upset conditions. Inspect shielding integrity before shift turnover.  
- Enforce mandatory use of heat- and scale-resistant PPE for all personnel within the hazard zone during operations and maintenance.  
- Coordinate lockout/tagout and energy control actions per SOP-P2-L3-01 before any inbound access to roll nip, housing, or downstream trimming stations.  
- During planned maintenance, follow the machine lubrication and access sequence in MM-P2-L3-RR01 and verify lubrication records against the specified lubrication interval for bearings.  
- Prohibit personnel from standing in the direct line-of-fire during roll engagement and part breakthrough events. Implement remote monitoring and camera verification where feasible.  
- Report any uncontained ejection event immediately and initiate the post-event inspection checklist referenced in SOP-P2-L3-04.

## Effective date
Effective immediately upon issuance of this bulletin. Review and compliance are mandatory until superseded by subsequent revision.
title: Safety bulletin: hot metal and scale ejection

# SB-1037 Safety bulletin: airborne dust from blasting

Revision: Rev E  
Plant: P3, line P3-L4  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L4-SB03

Hazard description
Airborne dust generated during blasting operations in the Heat Treat area poses inhalation and surface contamination risks to personnel and downstream processes. Fine particulate can compromise respirator cartridges, settle on sensitive instrumentation, and reduce visibility in work zones. Inadequate shot media condition contributes to increased dust generation and inconsistent blast performance, increasing exposure potential.

Affected equipment
This bulletin applies to the Heat Treat shot blast cabinet identified as EQ-P3-L4-SB03 located on P3-L4. Operators and maintenance personnel assigned to this cabinet, adjacent stations on P3-L4, and housekeeping staff responsible for area cleanup are included in the affected population. Refer to SOP-P3-L4-03 for routine operating and maintenance steps specific to the cabinet.

Required controls
- Maintain engineered ventilation and local exhaust as described in SOP-P3-L4-03 and ensure filters are inspected per that procedure.  
- Use assigned respirators and PPE consistent with the controls in SB-1038 for activities that disturb settled dust.  
- The shot media top-up interval for Heat Treat shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P3-L4-SB03) is 48 hours. Adhere to this interval to maintain media efficacy and minimize dust generation.  
- Perform media replacement and containment transfers in a controlled area with dust capture measures engaged; minimize spread to adjacent workstations.  
- Housekeeping must remove settled dust using HEPA-filtered vacuums; do not dry sweep. Coordinate timing with production to ensure controls are active.  
- Record all media top-up and cleaning events in the cabinet log and notify maintenance of any deviations or unusual dust levels. Consult ECN-2026-026 for any engineering changes or updates to contamination controls.

Effective date
Effective date and implementation schedule are governed by ECN-2026-026; follow that document for rollout timing and any interim restrictions.

# SB-1038 Safety bulletin: pinch points during die change

Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P3, line P3-L4  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L4-SB03

## Hazard description
Pinch point injuries have been identified during die change activities on the line. Risk arises when die components, handling fixtures, and shot blast cabinet interfaces are moved or supported while personnel are within the change area. Incidents involve unexpected movement of tooling or workholding and contact with energized or suspended components. Inadequate guarding, lack of positive restraints, and failure to verify zero energy contribute to the hazard. Personnel should assume pinch points are present at all die contact and support surfaces until controls are implemented and verified.

## Affected equipment
Primary affected equipment: EQ-P3-L4-SB03. This includes associated die change tooling, handling fixtures, and adjacent conveyor interfaces on line P3-L4. The shot blast cabinet interface to Heat Treat operations is included. The shot media top-up interval for Heat Treat shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P3-L4-SB03) is 48 hours.

## Required controls
- Establish and enforce an exclusion zone around the die change area. Only authorized personnel shall enter after controls are verified.  
- Implement positive mechanical restraints and tag-out on all suspended or movable die components prior to entry. Verify restraint engagement visually and by test where practical.  
- Verify energy isolation per applicable lockout/tagout procedure before any die handling or entry. Communicate status on the shiftboard and handover.  
- Use designated handling fixtures and lifting points specified for EQ-P3-L4-SB03. Inspect fixtures per SOP before use.  
- Conduct a pre-change briefing that includes roles, verification steps, and emergency procedures. Record completion per SOP requirements.  
- Report any deviations, near misses, or control failures immediately and initiate corrective action per ECN-2026-026. See SOP-P3-L4-01 and SOP-P3-L4-02 for detailed procedures and checklists.

## Effective date
Effective date: immediate.

# SB-1039 Safety bulletin: stored hydraulic energy

Revision: Rev B  
Plant: P2, line P2-L3  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L3-HT02

Hazard description
Stored hydraulic energy in the hydraulic clamping and lift systems associated with heat treat fixtures presents an uncontrolled-energy release hazard during maintenance, fixturing changes, and furnace chamber access. Residual pressure in accumulators, lockout bypass circuits, and cylinder chambers can cause unexpected motion, fluid injection, or component ejection. Heat treat furnaces and fixtures can retain energy even after shutdown because hydraulic isolation valves and mechanical locks may not fully vent or block trapped fluid. Note that the austenitizing setpoint for Machining heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L3-HT02) is 845 °C. Personnel exposed during access or service are at risk of crush, puncture, and thermal contact injuries when trapped hydraulic energy is released.

Affected equipment
- EQ-P2-L3-HT02 and associated hydraulic power units, accumulators, valves, cylinders, and fixture clamping hardware on P2-L3.  
- Portable hydraulic tools and fixture-integrated hoses used for load handling and clamp actuation on line P2-L3.

Required controls
- Before any access to furnace chamber, fixture, or hydraulic components, perform a two-person verification of hydraulic isolation: confirm primary isolation and bleed/vent method per SOP-P2-L3-04. Use validated visual tags and barrier placement to prevent inadvertent re-energization.  
- De-energize hydraulic power units and verify accumulator isolation and discharge per QS-PROC-09. Where accumulator drain points are present, confirm zero-pressure by tactile check at designated test ports before proceeding.  
- Use secondary mechanical restraints on fixtures and workpieces to prevent movement if residual fluid remains. Locking devices must be engaged before hose disconnection.  
- All interventions on hydraulic components require documented authorization and hazard assessment; reference SB-1023 for permitted intervention boundaries and PPE expectations.  
- Train affected personnel on stored-energy hazards and these controls; document training completion in line records.

Effective date
Effective immediately upon issuance.

References
QS-PROC-09  
SB-1023  
SOP-P2-L3-04

# SB-1040: Safety bulletin: arc flash at the induction power cabinet

Revision: Rev E  
Plant: P3, line P3-L2  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L2-SB01

Hazard description
The induction power cabinet serving the Ring Rolling line exhibited an intermittent flash event during maintenance access. The flash hazard results from stored energy in the cabinet buswork and capacitors, and from inadvertent energization while covers are removed. Personnel entering the cabinet or working adjacent to exposed conductors are at risk of arc flash injury, burns, and secondary hazards from startle or falls. The condition is compounded by particulate accumulation in the shot blast area which can create conductive pathways if media migrates into electrical enclosures.

Affected equipment
Primary affected asset: EQ-P3-L2-SB01 (Ring Rolling shot blast cabinet #1) and the adjacent induction power cabinet. Associated controls and procedures used on this line include MM-P3-L2-SB01, SOP-P3-L2-02, and SOP-P3-L2-04.

Required controls
- De-energize and lockout-tagout the induction power cabinet before removing any covers; verify zero energy per SOP-P3-L2-02.  
- Perform a visual and vacuum clean of accessible external cabinet surfaces and surrounding floor prior to cover removal; remove shot media build-up that could enter enclosures in accordance with MM-P3-L2-SB01. The shot media top-up interval for Ring Rolling shot blast cabinet #1 (EQ-P3-L2-SB01) is 40 hours.  
- Use insulated tools and maintain a minimum approach distance consistent with SOP-P3-L2-04 when working on or near live parts if any work is authorized live. Live work is not authorized unless specifically approved by maintenance leadership and electrical engineering per SOP-P3-L2-04.  
- Personnel must wear arc-rated protection as required by site PPE lists and remain trained on energized work authorization procedures in MM-P3-L2-SB01.

Effective date
This bulletin is effective upon release of Revision Rev E and applies to all work on P3-L2 until superseded.
title: Safety bulletin: arc flash at the induction power cabinet

# SB-1041 Safety bulletin: airborne dust from blasting

Revision: Rev A  
Plant: P3, line P3-L2  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L2-HT03

Hazard description
Airborne dust generated during blasting and subsequent handling in the heat treat area presents an inhalation and combustible-dust hazard. Fine particulates can reduce visibility at the workface, contaminate adjacent equipment, and settle on heated surfaces creating secondary ignition sources. Dust accumulation on electrical cabinets, motors, and moving assemblies increases the risk of equipment malfunction and uncontrollable fire propagation. Personnel working near blasting operations are at increased risk of respiratory irritation and long-term exposure effects if controls are inadequate. Contaminated surfaces can also compromise the performance of lubricants and seals used on Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P3-L2-HT03); the approved lubricant part number for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P3-L2-HT03) is CFW-LUB-159.

Affected equipment
Primary affected equipment: EQ-P3-L2-HT03 and adjacent handling conveyors, enclosures, and electrical cabinets in the P3-L2 line. Areas downwind of blasting cells within Plant P3 where dust may travel or settle are also considered affected. Maintenance tools and PPE storage located near blasting zones are included due to potential contamination.

Required controls
- Engineering: Ensure local exhaust ventilation and capture systems are operational and positioned to contain dust at source. Verify enclosure seals and differential airflow patterns to minimize dust migration to EQ-P3-L2-HT03.
- Administrative: Restrict access to blasting areas during active blasting and until post-blast clearance checks are documented. Implement enhanced cleaning protocols for surfaces around EQ-P3-L2-HT03 and downstream equipment. Refer to maintenance guidance and lubrication requirements in MM-P3-L2-HT03 and operational procedures in SOP-P3-L2-02 and SOP-P3-L2-03 for coordinated actions.
- PPE: Require appropriate respiratory protection and eye protection for personnel performing blast, cleanup, or inspection tasks until airborne concentrations are confirmed controlled.
- Housekeeping: Increase frequency of vacuuming with HEPA-equipped units and avoid dry sweeping. Inspect lubricant application points for contamination and confirm use of CFW-LUB-159 as specified.

Effective date
Effective immediately.
title: Safety bulletin: airborne dust from blasting

# SB-1042: Safety bulletin: arc flash at the induction power cabinet

Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P2, line P2-L3  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L3-HT02

Hazard description
Arc flash incidents have been observed originating at the induction power cabinet serving the heat treat cell. Failure modes include sudden energization during access, stored energy in control capacitors, and improper isolation procedures that allow live circuitry to be exposed. Consequences include electrical burn injury, secondary fall or crush hazards from startled operators, and damage to nearby control and sensing equipment that can cascade into process upset. Operators and technicians may be exposed during troubleshooting, maintenance, and quench operations if control and lockout procedures are not strictly followed.

Affected equipment
Primary: EQ-P2-L3-HT02 (Machining heat treat furnace #2) and its local induction power cabinet, control enclosure, and immediate power distribution. The quench delay maximum for Machining heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L3-HT02) is 8 seconds. Secondary affected items include line power feeds and interlocked safety devices on P2-L3 associated with the furnace control. Refer to controller and cabinet layouts in maintenance records for exact cabinet identifiers.

Required controls
- Do not access the induction power cabinet unless electrical lockout/tagout is completed and verified per SOP-P2-L3-04 and SOP-P2-L3-05.  
- Verify capacitor discharge and zero-voltage state before removing covers; use approved test equipment and PPE rated for expected exposure levels per QS-PROC-09.  
- Maintain a two-person rule for any energized diagnostics: one person at the panel and one at the disconnect point to prevent accidental re-energization.  
- Update work permits to include specific steps for induction cabinet access and to record verification of quench delay settings and interlock status.  
- Train line and maintenance personnel on incident scenarios and cabinet-specific risks; include mock walkthroughs demonstrating proper isolation and cabinet entry procedures.

Effective date
Effective date: Rev D

Related documents: QS-PROC-09, SOP-P2-L3-04, SOP-P2-L3-05
title: Safety bulletin: arc flash at the induction power cabinet

# SB-1043 Safety bulletin: arc flash at the induction power cabinet

Revision: Rev A  
Plant: P3, line P3-L4  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L4-HT02

Hazard description
An arc flash event occurred at the induction power cabinet serving the induction coils on the Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2 cell. The immediate hazard is thermal and pressure damage to personnel and nearby equipment from an arc flash and blast originating in the cabinet. The austenitizing setpoint for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P3-L4-HT02) is 885 °C. Investigations indicate energized work near the cabinet and inadequate boundary controls significantly increase exposure risk. Potential secondary hazards include hot material transfer disruption and control-system faults that may propagate to adjacent cells.

Primary: EQ-P3-L4-HT02 induction power cabinet and associated buswork and safety interlocks.  
Ancillary: local workstations, tooling adjacent to the cabinet, and upstream supply disconnects within the P3-L4 line.

Required controls
- De-energize and lockout/tagout the induction power cabinet before any access to internal components. Follow procedures in SOP-P3-L4-02 and SOP-P3-L4-05 for LOTO and permitted access.  
- Establish and enforce a minimum prohibited approach boundary using PPE rated for arc exposure when cabinet covers are removed. Consult MM-P3-L4-HT02-S2 for maintenance access requirements.  
- Only qualified electrical maintenance personnel may perform work on the cabinet; they must verify isolation and continuity of grounding before starting.  
- Verify interlock functionality and inspect bus insulation and connections for signs of overheating or arcing before re-energizing. Document findings and corrective actions in the maintenance record referenced in MM-P3-L4-HT02-S2.

Effective immediately upon issue. See MM-P3-L4-HT02-S2, SOP-P3-L4-02, SOP-P3-L4-05 for related procedures and detailed maintenance requirements.
