text:
# SB-1044: Safety bulletin: hot metal and scale ejection

Revision: Rev E  
Plant: P3, line P3-L1  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L1-IH03

Hazard description
Hot metal and attached scale present a risk of sudden ejection during charging, dwell, and transfer operations at the induction billet heater. Ejected material can strike personnel, damage fixtures, and initiate secondary metal spatter or fires. Scale detachment is unpredictable when billets are at operating temperature and when mechanical disturbance or misalignment occurs. The target billet temperature for Hot Forge induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P3-L1-IH03) is 1260 °C. Operations that expose heated billets to drafts, impact, or tooling interference increase the likelihood of scale liberation and ballistic trajectories of hot fragments.

Affected equipment
EQ-P3-L1-IH03 and any adjacent handling, charging, or transfer devices servicing this induction heater are in scope. Attached fixtures, manipulators, charging tongs, and immediate workstations positioned within the ejection envelope around EQ-P3-L1-IH03 are considered affected. Related procedural controls are documented in MM-P3-L1-IH03, SOP-P3-L1-01, and SOP-P3-L1-05.

Required controls
- Restrict access to the immediate ejection envelope around EQ-P3-L1-IH03 during heating, charging, and transfer activities. Post signage and barrier delineation consistent with plant access policy.  
- Require full PPE for exposed personnel as defined in SOP-P3-L1-05 and prohibit work inside the envelope unless tasks are specifically authorized by the shift lead and documented per MM-P3-L1-IH03.  
- Perform pre-charge inspection of billets for loose scale and surface defects; any suspect billet must be processed according to SOP-P3-L1-01.  
- Use tool and fixture standoff practices that minimize disturbance of scale during insertion and extraction and ensure alignment before engagement.  
- Ensure emergency stop and guarding systems for EQ-P3-L1-IH03 are functional and verified per MM-P3-L1-IH03 before filling operations commence.

Effective date
This bulletin is effective immediately on issue and applies to all activities involving EQ-P3-L1-IH03 until superseded.
title: Safety bulletin: hot metal and scale ejection

text:
# SB-1045 - Safety bulletin: airborne dust from blasting
Revision: Rev E  
Plant: P2, line P2-L3  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L3-HT02

Hazard description
- Blasting operations within the P2-L3 cell have generated airborne respirable dust that migrates into adjacent machining and heat treat areas. Airborne dust increases inhalation risk and contamination of process equipment, with potential to affect finished part integrity and personnel respiratory safety. The quench delay maximum for Machining heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L3-HT02) is 8 seconds. Dust accumulation on fixtures, sensors, and filtration intakes can degrade process control and may prolong quench exposure if maintenance access is impeded.

Affected equipment
- Primary affected equipment: EQ-P2-L3-HT02 (Machining heat treat furnace #2).  
- Affected location: Plant P2, line P2-L3.  
- Secondary impact: adjacent blasting booths, part handling conveyors, and local extraction units serving P2-L3.

Required controls
- Implement local containment at blasting source: ensure blast booth curtains and door seals are maintained intact and positioned to prevent cross-flow into P2-L3 machining/heat treat zones.
- Increase capture ventilation at the blasting location and verify negative pressure relationships relative to EQ-P2-L3-HT02 work envelope before restarting operations.
- Perform targeted housekeeping on exterior surfaces of EQ-P2-L3-HT02 and surrounding conveyors to remove settled dust using HEPA-filtered vacuums; avoid compressed air blow-down.
- Inspect and verify filtration and sensor housings on EQ-P2-L3-HT02 are free of external deposits prior to heat treatment cycles to prevent process interference with the 8 seconds quench delay maximum.
- Personal protective equipment: enforce respirator use in affected zones per site PPE matrix; post area signage to restrict non-essential entry.
- Record all corrective actions and inspections in the maintenance log for P2-L3; escalate recurring contamination to the Plant P2 safety committee.

References
- See SB-1023, SB-1039, SOP-P2-L3-01 for related procedures and prior corrective actions.

Effective date
- Effective immediately upon issuance.
title: Safety bulletin: airborne dust from blasting

text:
# SB-1046 Safety bulletin: noise exposure

Revision: Rev B  
Plant: P1, line P1-L4  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L4-CN01

Hazard description
This bulletin addresses elevated noise exposure risk associated with machining and heat-treat operations on the line. Intermittent high-impact contact events, bearing wear, and insufficient lubrication at the turning center can increase airborne noise and impulsive noise events that exceed allowable exposure for personnel working at or adjacent to the cell. Chronic exposure to elevated noise can cause permanent hearing damage and reduces situational awareness, increasing overall safety risk.

Affected equipment
Primary affected asset: EQ-P1-L4-CN01 (Heat Treat CNC turning center #1). Ancillary exposure applies to operators, setup technicians, maintenance staff, and nearby line personnel who perform loading, unloading, setup, or inspection activities within the P1-L4 work envelope. The way lube refill interval for Heat Treat CNC turning center #1 (EQ-P1-L4-CN01) is 40 hours.

Required controls
- Administrative: Limit duration of close-proximity tasks and rotate personnel away from the immediate cell during heavy machining periods. Refer to SOP-P1-L4-02 for permitted access and allowed presence protocols.  
- Engineering: Ensure acoustic panels and enclosures are present and maintained per MM-P1-L4-CN01. Verify seals and guards are in place to reduce radiated noise before resuming production.  
- Maintenance: Prioritize inspection of drive bearings, waylubrication system, and cutting tool condition to reduce mechanical noise sources. Update maintenance activities in accordance with MM-P1-L4-CN01. Replace or repair components showing abnormal noise before resuming normal operations.  
- PPE: Require hearing protection for all personnel entering the immediate cell area. Supervisors must enforce PPE use and document compliance per SOP-P1-L4-05.  
- Verification: Conduct noise monitoring and post-repair acoustic checks following actions and record results in maintenance logs referenced by MM-P1-L4-CN01.

Effective date
Effective immediately.
title: Safety bulletin: noise exposure

text:
# SB-1047: Safety bulletin: arc flash at the induction power cabinet

Revision: Rev B  
Plant: P3, line P3-L1  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L1-IH03

Hazard description
- A recent field incident identified an arc flash originating in the induction power cabinet associated with the Hot Forge induction billet heater. The event occurred during a maintenance access activity while the power cabinet was energized. Energized-component exposure, inadequate verification of de-energized state, and degraded component insulation contributed to a flash and subsequent minor burns and equipment damage. The primary hazards are thermal injury from arc flash, flying molten metal/debris, and secondary ignition of nearby materials. Refer to ECN-2026-010 and SB-1044 for background on the root-cause assessment and previous cabinet-related safety actions.

Affected equipment
- Hot Forge induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P3-L1-IH03) power cabinet and associated disconnects, control wiring, and adjacent panels on line P3-L1.
- All maintenance, troubleshooting, and setup activities that require access to the cabinet interior or adjacent energized components. See SOP-P3-L1-05 for permitted maintenance steps and lockout/tagout protocol.

Required controls
- Do not access or open the induction power cabinet while it is energized. Verify de-energized condition per SOP-P3-L1-05 before any entry or internal work.
- The coil cooling water flow minimum for Hot Forge induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P3-L1-IH03) is 65 L/min. Maintain continuous flow at or above this minimum to prevent coil overheating that can degrade insulation and increase arc-flash risk.
- Perform pre-access visual inspections for signs of insulation breakdown, discoloration, or abnormal odors; report any deficiencies and isolate equipment until repaired.
- Use full arc-rated PPE and distance-rated barriers whenever energized work cannot be avoided. Apply two-person verification for de-energization and reinstatement procedures.
- Implement a cabinet maintenance checklist and documented verification steps; include acceptance by maintenance supervisor and safety representative prior to re-energizing.

Effective date
- Effective immediately upon issue. Review and incorporate controls into routine maintenance and permit-to-work processes; reference ECN-2026-010, SB-1044, and SOP-P3-L1-05 for related corrective actions and procedures.
title: Safety bulletin: arc flash at the induction power cabinet

# SB-1048 Safety bulletin: airborne dust from blasting

## Hazard description
Blasting operations on P2, line P2-L4 generate respirable and nuisance airborne dust that can migrate into adjacent work areas and process equipment. Dust accumulation presents inhalation risk to personnel, potential contamination of metallurgical processes, and increased housekeeping burden. Particular concern exists for the heat treat area where fugitive dust can enter heat treat equipment and compromise part cleanliness and furnace atmosphere control. The lubricant part number for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L4-HT02) is CFW-LUB-426.

## Affected equipment
- EQ-P2-L4-HT02 located on P2, line P2-L4.
- Adjacent conveyors, masking stations, and temporary staging areas downwind of blasting.
- Personnel performing blasting, masking, cleanup, material handling, and heat treat loading/unloading operations.

## Required controls
- Implement local exhaust ventilation at blasting booths and transfer points to capture fugitive dust before it migrates toward P2, line P2-L4 heat treat areas. Coordinate ventilation modifications with maintenance per MM-P2-L4-HT02 before implementation.
- Establish barriering and controlled access routes between blasting and heat treat zones; require visual confirmation of barriers prior to blasting.
- Update SOP-P2-L4-03 to include pre-blast checks for dust containment, post-blast cleanup procedures, and communication steps to heat treat personnel responsible for EQ-P2-L4-HT02.
- Use designated cleaning methods that prevent resuspension of particulate into air streams; collect and dispose of blasting media and settled dust per ECN-2026-020 engineering change guidance.
- Verify that lubricant and maintenance activities for EQ-P2-L4-HT02 reference CFW-LUB-426 when preparing furnace servicing to avoid cross-contamination from incompatible materials.
- Require supervisors to document control implementation and close nonconformances using existing plant forms; escalate unresolved control barriers to plant management.

## Effective date
Rev A
title: Safety bulletin: airborne dust from blasting

# SB-1049 — Safety bulletin: pinch points during die change
Revision: Rev A  
Plant: P2, line P2-L2  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L2-RR03

Hazard description
During die change operations on the ring rolling machine, exposed moving interfaces and closing clearances create pinch-point hazards. Operators and maintenance staff are at risk of hand and limb entrapment when dies, adapters, or workpieces shift unexpectedly while jammed components are being freed, fasteners are being loosened, or during preliminary alignment. Residual stored energy in roll actuators and gravity loads on dies can cause uncontrolled motion. Visibility is limited in the die pocket area, increasing the chance of unintentional contact with moving surfaces.

Affected equipment
This bulletin applies to the Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #3 identified as EQ-P2-L2-RR03 located on line P2-L2 at plant P2. Refer to MM-P2-L2-RR03 and MM-P2-L2-RR03-S2 for maintenance history and component layouts. Related safety precedents: SB-1017.

Required controls
- Establish and enforce written die change procedures specific to EQ-P2-L2-RR03 that require isolation of all energy sources and confirmation of zero-clearance condition before hands enter the die pocket.  
- Apply lockout/tagout and physical blocking of any component capable of translating, rotating, or dropping into the die zone; ensure tags remain visible for the duration of the work.  
- Use purpose-designed lifting and holding fixtures rated for die mass; secure fixtures to prevent lateral shift.  
- Restrict die change tasks to authorized personnel who have completed documented training and competency verification on the procedure for EQ-P2-L2-RR03.  
- Maintain clear communication between equipment operator and maintenance staff using positive confirmation practices; use agreed visual and verbal signals prior to any motion.  
- Inspect guards, interlocks, and blocking devices before each die change; log findings per the maintenance procedure references MM-P2-L2-RR03 and MM-P2-L2-RR03-S2.  
- Note for maintenance planning: The main roll bearing lubrication interval for Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #3 (EQ-P2-L2-RR03) is 185 hours. Include lubrication status in pre-change checklist.

Effective date
Effective immediately.
title: Safety bulletin: pinch points during die change

text:
# SB-1050 Safety bulletin: stored hydraulic energy

Revision: Rev B  
Plant: P3, line P3-L1  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L1-IH03

Hazard description
Stored hydraulic energy associated with the coil retention and clamping systems on the induction billet heater can release unexpectedly during coil change, maintenance, or emergency shut-down. Release of stored hydraulic energy can cause rapid movement of coil assemblies, dislodgement of guarding, or high-energy fluid ejection, creating a risk of crush, impact, or fluid injection injuries to maintenance and operations personnel. Residual energy can persist after isolation of electrical power if hydraulic reservoirs, accumulators, or line charge are not depleted or mechanically restrained.

Affected equipment
This bulletin applies to Hot Forge induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P3-L1-IH03) located on P3-L1. The coil cooling water flow minimum for Hot Forge induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P3-L1-IH03) is 65 L/min. Refer to MM-P3-L1-IH03 for the maintenance history and component locations and to SOP-P3-L1-01 for standard lockout/tagout steps specific to P3-L1 induction equipment.

Required controls
- Prior to any work where hydraulic circuits, fittings, or actuators may be exposed or manipulated, verify mechanical restraints are installed and load-bearing elements are supported.  
- Depressurize and isolate hydraulic circuits per SOP-P3-L1-01. Confirm depleted state of hydraulic accumulators and reservoirs before removing fittings or covers.  
- Use procedural checks in MM-P3-L1-IH03 to confirm completion of hydraulic isolation tasks; document completion on the maintenance record.  
- Personnel conducting work must be trained and authorized for hydraulic energy hazards and must use rated protective equipment and barrier systems appropriate for stored-energy exposures.  
- Report any unplanned release events through ECN-2026-006 and suspend related work until root cause and corrective actions are implemented.

Effective date
Effective: Immediate.
title: Safety bulletin: stored hydraulic energy

# QS-PROC-02 Quench and temper process window (P1)

Revision: Rev C  
Plant: P1, line P1-L2  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L2-IH02

Scope
This quality specification defines the process window limits and verification requirements for the quench and temper operation performed on parts originating from Ring Rolling induction billet heater #2 (EQ-P1-L2-IH02) on line P1-L2. It applies to material handling, heat-treatment transfer, and documented verification prior to quench. Related procedures: SOP-P1-L2-01, SOP-P1-L2-03, SOP-P1-L2-05.

Requirements table

| Requirement | Specification | Reference |
|---|---|---|
| Billet charging temperature | The target billet temperature for Ring Rolling induction billet heater #2 (EQ-P1-L2-IH02) is 1230 °C. | SOP-P1-L2-01 |
| Temperature verification at transfer | Confirm recorded heater output equals specified billet charging temperature prior to transfer to quench station. | SOP-P1-L2-03 |
| Documentation | Log heater ID, operator initials, and reference to this specification in batch record prior to quench. | SOP-P1-L2-05 |

Inspection method
Inspectors shall verify the heater output record in the batch file and confirm the entry for EQ-P1-L2-IH02 matches the specified billet charging temperature in this document. Verify presence of the heater ID and the process note referencing this specification. Inspection is performed by review of the electronic batch record and cross-check of the physical log where applicable. Non-destructive verification instrumentation records shall be retained with the job folder and cross-referenced to SOP-P1-L2-01.

Nonconformance handling
If recorded heater output for EQ-P1-L2-IH02 does not match the specified billet charging temperature in this document, stop the quench step and isolate the affected batch. Notify Quality and the line supervisor, attach the deviation to the batch record, and follow corrective action steps in SOP-P1-L2-05. Release of affected parts requires documented disposition by Quality per SOP-P1-L2-03.
title: Quench and temper process window (P1)

text:
# QS-PROC-03 Ring rolling dimensional control (P1)
Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P1, line P1-L2  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L2-HT03

Scope
This quality specification applies to ring rolling operations and subsequent heat treatment control for parts processed on line P1-L2. It defines dimensional acceptance criteria, inspection methods, and nonconformance handling for rings processed on EQ-P1-L2-HT03. The austenitizing setpoint for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P1-L2-HT03) is 855 °C. Refer to MM-P1-L2-HT03 for equipment maintenance, SB-1035 for material-specific guidance, and SOP-P1-L2-04 for measurement setup.

Requirements table
| Feature | Requirement | Acceptance |
|---|---:|---|
| Outer diameter (OD) | Measured per SOP-P1-L2-04 | Conforms to document criteria in SOP-P1-L2-04 |
| Inner diameter (ID) | Measured per SOP-P1-L2-04 | Conforms to document criteria in SOP-P1-L2-04 |
| Axial thickness | Measured per SOP-P1-L2-04 | Conforms to document criteria in SOP-P1-L2-04 |
| Roundness and runout | Measured per SOP-P1-L2-04 | Conforms to document criteria in SOP-P1-L2-04 |
| Metallurgical state | Austenitizing performed on EQ-P1-L2-HT03 | Austenitizing setpoint 855 °C applied and recorded per MM-P1-L2-HT03 |

Inspection method
Inspection is performed following SOP-P1-L2-04. Calibration of measuring instruments must be current and traceable as recorded in MM-P1-L2-HT03. Dimensional checks are performed at locations and frequencies specified in SOP-P1-L2-04. Measurement data shall be entered into the production inspection record and retained per plant record control. For heat treat verification, furnace control logs shall show the austenitizing setpoint of 855 °C for affected heat cycles; cross-reference furnace log entries to parts processed during the same cycle.

Nonconformance handling
If a ring fails to meet the acceptance criteria in the Requirements table, tag and segregate affected parts and notify quality. Initiate an investigation per SB-1035 and follow containment actions in SOP-P1-L2-04. For any heat treat deviation where the austenitizing setpoint of 855 °C was not achieved or recorded on EQ-P1-L2-HT03, quarantine the lot and run corrective actions per MM-P1-L2-HT03 and SB-1035.
title: Ring rolling dimensional control (P1)

text:
# QS-PROC-04 Shot peening coverage (P1)
Revision: Rev C  
Plant: P1, line P1-L3  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L3-IH01

Scope
This quality specification defines shot peening coverage requirements and related controls for parts processed on line P1-L3 using equipment EQ-P1-L3-IH01. It includes acceptance criteria, required evidence, and links to related documentation ECN-2026-029, SB-1026, SOP-P1-L3-05. The coil cooling water flow minimum for Machining induction billet heater #1 (EQ-P1-L3-IH01) is 79 L/min.

Requirements table
| Requirement | Acceptance criteria | Reference |
|-------------|---------------------|-----------|
| Shot peening coverage | Full visual evidence of specified coverage per part family and routing | SOP-P1-L3-05 |
| Media condition | Media free of contaminant and within acceptable degradation limits per maintenance log | SB-1026 |
| Machine setup | Machine parameters match approved change records and ECN documents | ECN-2026-029 |
| Cooling supply | Coil cooling water flow meets minimum for heater EQ-P1-L3-IH01 | EQ-P1-L3-IH01 spec sheet, this document |

Inspection method
Inspectors shall verify shot peening coverage using visual and photographic evidence on the shop floor immediately after peening. Records shall reference the part identifier and the operating checklist from SOP-P1-L3-05. Confirm that media condition is recorded and cross-checked against SB-1026 guidelines. Verify that machine setup corresponds to the latest approved configuration in ECN-2026-029. Confirm coil cooling water flow minimum for Machining induction billet heater #1 (EQ-P1-L3-IH01) is documented in the equipment log and meets the value specified in this document.

Nonconformance handling
Nonconforming coverage or media condition requires containment: affected parts are segregated and tagged, process is stopped until corrective action is implemented, and root cause is documented. Notify process engineering and reference ECN-2026-029 for disposition of affected batches. Repeat failures trigger a review of SOP-P1-L3-05 and maintenance actions per SB-1026.
title: Shot peening coverage (P1)

text:
# QS-PROC-05 Machining surface finish (P1)
Revision: Rev B  
Plant: P1, line P1-L4  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L4-HT03

Scope
This quality specification defines required surface finish acceptance criteria, related process constraints, and inspection methods for components machined on line P1-L4 and processed through Heat Treat heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P1-L4-HT03). Applicable to production and maintenance personnel controlling feed-into and output from EQ-P1-L4-HT03. Refer to ECN-2026-002 for design tolerance updates and SOP-P1-L4-01 and SOP-P1-L4-02 for process execution.

Requirements table

| Item | Requirement |
|---|---|
| Surface finish acceptance | See machine program and drawing per ECN-2026-002 |
| Heat treat quench control | The quench delay maximum for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P1-L4-HT03) is 15 seconds. |
| Process documentation | All runs must be recorded per SOP-P1-L4-01 and SOP-P1-L4-02 |
| Equipment condition | EQ-P1-L4-HT03 must be verified operational per SOP-P1-L4-02 before use |

Inspection method
Inspect finished parts per sampling and acceptance criteria in SOP-P1-L4-01. Visual and profilometer checks shall be performed at the first-piece inspection and after any process interruption. For parts passing through EQ-P1-L4-HT03, verify quench delay using furnace event log and operator checklist recorded in the part traveler. Record any deviation from the quench delay requirement and tag affected lots for review. Retain inspection records with the job packet as required by SOP-P1-L4-01.

Nonconformance handling
Nonconforming parts or process records are to be isolated and dispositioned following SOP-P1-L4-02. Report nonconformance referencing QS-PROC-05 and ECN-2026-002. For any instance where the quench delay exceeds the stated requirement for EQ-P1-L4-HT03, initiate containment, perform root cause analysis, and implement corrective action per SOP-P1-L4-02. Rework or scrap decisions shall be documented and approved by Quality.
title: Machining surface finish (P1)

text:
# QS-PROC-06: Forging temperature control (P2)
Revision: Rev E  
Plant: P2, line P2-L1  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L1-IH02

Scope
This quality specification defines the requirements and verification method for induction billet heater control on EQ-P2-L1-IH02 to ensure consistent forging temperature input to the hot forge line at P2-L1. Applies to operations, maintenance, and quality personnel responsible for process control and inspection.

Requirements table
| Item | Requirement | Acceptance |
|---|---|---|
| Coil cooling water flow | The coil cooling water flow minimum for Hot Forge induction billet heater #2 (EQ-P2-L1-IH02) is 55 L/min. | Flow reading meets or exceeds specified minimum |
| Process control signal integrity | Control signals to EQ-P2-L1-IH02 shall be functional and free of obvious faults. Refer to SOP-P2-L1-02 for control verification steps. | No alarm or fault present during verification |
| Recordkeeping | All flow readings and corrective actions shall be recorded per SOP-P2-L1-03. | Records complete and legible in the process log |

Inspection method
- Verify coil cooling water flow on EQ-P2-L1-IH02 using the calibrated flowmeter located upstream of the coil. Record the instrument reading and compare to the requirement in the table.
- Confirm control signal integrity by following the sequence in SOP-P2-L1-02 and observing for alarms or faults while the equipment is in normal operating mode.
- Inspect the process log and record entries per SOP-P2-L1-03 to ensure traceability of each measurement and any maintenance actions taken.

Nonconformance handling
- If the coil cooling water flow on EQ-P2-L1-IH02 is below the requirement specified in this document, tag the equipment out of production and initiate corrective action per SOP-P2-L1-03.
- Document the nonconformance in the quality system and include supporting data from the inspection method. Notify line supervision and maintenance according to plant escalation practices.
- Re-inspect and record results after corrective action completion. Close nonconformance only when all acceptance criteria in this document are met.

Related documents: ECN-2026-039, SOP-P2-L1-02, SOP-P2-L1-03
title: Forging temperature control (P2)

text:
# QS-PROC-07 Quench and temper process window (P2) Rev B

Scope
This quality specification defines the process window and controls for quench and temper operations on parts produced at Plant P2, line P2-L2 using equipment EQ-P2-L2-IH01. It specifies required inputs, monitoring points, and references for operators and quality engineers.

| Plant / Line | P2 / P2-L2 |
| Equipment | EQ-P2-L2-IH01 |
| Lubricant part number for Ring Rolling induction billet heater #1 | CFW-LUB-938 |

Inspection consists of review of the production batch record and the electronic process log for the run. text:
# QS-PROC-08 Ring rolling dimensional control (P2)
Revision: Rev C  
Plant: P2, line P2-L2  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L2-HT02

## Scope
This quality specification defines dimensional control requirements for ring rolling operations performed on EQ-P2-L2-HT02 at plant P2, line P2-L2. It applies to all ring geometries processed for dimensional acceptance and ties into heat-treat furnace maintenance where lubricant identification is required: The lubricant part number for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L2-HT02) is CFW-LUB-376.

## Requirements table
| Feature | Requirement | Acceptance |
|---|---:|---|
| Out-of-roundness | Must be evaluated against drawing characteristics | Accept per drawing note and customer requirement |
| Wall thickness uniformity | Must be inspected across circumference | Accept when consistent with process capability and drawing callout |
| Inside diameter | Measure after final sizing | Accept per drawing datum and inspection record |
| Surface condition | No tearing or laps that affect fit or function | Reject if mode of failure compromises performance |
| Identification | Parts must be traceable to heat/lot | Accept when traceability maintained per SOP-P2-L2-04 |

Refer to ECN-2026-028 and ECN-2026-031 for engineering changes that affect dimensional criteria and tooling setup.

## Inspection method
Inspection shall be performed using calibrated gauges and metrology equipment appropriate for the feature. Record inspection results on the job traveler and link to the part lot. Compare findings to the current controlled drawing. For features affected by ECN-2026-028 or ECN-2026-031, apply the revised criteria in those documents. Use SOP-P2-L2-04 for documentation and traceability procedures. Where nonconforming features are borderline, escalate to quality engineering for disposition.

## Nonconformance handling
Nonconforming parts shall be segregated and labeled. Initiate a nonconformance report and notify production and quality leads. Disposition options include rework, return to engineering for exception, or scrap following documented approval. Corrective actions shall reference ECN-2026-028, ECN-2026-031, and SOP-P2-L2-04 as applicable. Records of dispositions and corrective actions shall be retained per plant document retention policy.
title: Ring rolling dimensional control (P2)

text:
# ECN-2026-001 - Change notice - Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2

Revision: Rev A  
Plant: P3, line P3-L4  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L4-HT02

Reason for change
- Production change request identified inconsistent quench timing logs on EQ-P3-L4-HT02 that exceeded established process tolerance. A process limits review determined the control setpoint and operator procedure did not explicitly require a maximum allowable quench delay. This ECN establishes the maximum quench delay to align equipment control, operator actions, and inspection acceptance criteria and to reduce rework and post-heat-treat rejects.
- The quench delay maximum for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P3-L4-HT02) is 20 seconds.

Affected items
- Standard operating procedures: SOP-P3-L4-02, SOP-P3-L4-04, SOP-P3-L4-05 need revision to incorporate the quench delay requirement, clarify operator responsibilities during loading/unloading, and update hold points for inspection.
- Equipment program: EQ-P3-L4-HT02 PLC program and HMI displays where quench initiation and delay timers are logged.
- Training materials and operator checklists associated with furnace operation, part traceability records, and in-process inspection forms tied to SOP-P3-L4-02, SOP-P3-L4-04, SOP-P3-L4-05.

Implementation
- Update documents SOP-P3-L4-02, SOP-P3-L4-04, SOP-P3-L4-05 to include the quench delay requirement and the measurement/control method. Include explicit action steps for operators when a potential delay is anticipated.
- Modify EQ-P3-L4-HT02 PLC/HMI to alarm and log any quench initiation delay exceeding the specified maximum. Incorporate visible timer and deviation flag on operator screens.
- Execute a controlled rollout: revise procedures, implement PLC/HMI changes, and conduct operator training and competency assessment referencing the updated SOPs prior to release to production.
- Update inspection checklists to require verification of adherence to the quench delay requirement for affected lots.

Approvals
- Engineering approval required for PLC/HMI changes and procedural text updates referencing SOP-P3-L4-02, SOP-P3-L4-04, SOP-P3-L4-05.
- Operations management approval required for training completion and release to production.
- Quality assurance approval required for checklist and acceptance criteria updates.
title: Change notice - Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2

text:
# ECN-2026-002 Change notice - Heat Treat heat treat furnace #3

Revision: Rev A  
Plant: P1, line P1-L4  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L4-HT03

## Reason for change
Review of process capability and metallurgical verification identified that the documented austenitizing setpoint deviated from the process control reference. To align furnace control, process documentation, and shop floor operation, the setpoint for EQ-P1-L4-HT03 is being standardized. This change reduces variability in microstructure outcomes and supports conformance to customer material specifications.

## Affected items
- Heat Treat heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P1-L4-HT03) control recipe and operator checklist.  
- Master maintenance log entries associated with EQ-P1-L4-HT03.  
- Work instructions and training materials used by P1, line P1-L4 operators.  
- Quality records where furnace setpoint is referenced.

The austenitizing setpoint for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P1-L4-HT03) is 880 °C.

Reference procedures impacted: MM-P1-L4-HT03-S3, QS-PROC-05, SOP-P1-L4-03.

## Implementation
Update the furnace control recipe to reflect the setpoint indicated above. Revise operator checklist and SOP-P1-L4-03 to reflect the standardized value and ensure training material mirrors the updated control recipe. Maintenance team to verify setpoint configuration in the control system and record confirmation in MM-P1-L4-HT03-S3. Quality to update process control plans and record verification actions under QS-PROC-05. Post-implementation validation runs shall be documented and accepted by operations and quality prior to returning to standard production.

## Approvals
Requested approvals from Operations, Maintenance, and Quality are required to complete the change and close the ECN. Approvers will confirm updates to control recipe, SOP-P1-L4-03, and records in MM-P1-L4-HT03-S3 and QS-PROC-05.
title: Change notice - Heat Treat heat treat furnace #3

text:
# ECN-2026-005 - Change notice - Machining induction billet heater #1

Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P1, line P1-L3  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L3-IH01

## Reason for change
Operational monitoring identified recurring thermal excursions correlated with reduced coil cooling water flow for Machining induction billet heater #1 (EQ-P1-L3-IH01). Analysis of field data and manufacturer guidance indicates the coil requires a defined minimum cooling flow to maintain safe and reliable operation. This change clarifies the required minimum coil cooling water flow to prevent premature coil degradation and unplanned downtime.

## Affected items
- Machining induction billet heater #1 (EQ-P1-L3-IH01) coil assembly and associated cooling circuit on line P1-L3.  
- Operator procedures and maintenance checklists referencing cooling flow setpoints in the equipment documentation and SOPs.

## Implementation
The coil cooling water flow minimum for Machining induction billet heater #1 (EQ-P1-L3-IH01) is 79 L/min. Update control system interlocks, alarm thresholds, and operator displays to reflect the minimum flow requirement. Revise SOP-P1-L3-05 to include verification of the minimum coil cooling water flow before heater start and during process operation; reference ECN-2026-046 for related electrical interlock changes; reference SB-1026 for supplemental safety bulletin instructions. Maintenance to confirm flow sensor calibration and piping integrity prior to returning equipment to service. Training for affected operators and maintenance personnel will be scheduled to review the updated flow requirement and revised procedural steps. Document traceability of the implementation steps and evidence of completed updates within the document control system.

## Approvals
Engineering acknowledges the change and confirms technical validity based on field analysis and supplier guidance. Operations endorses the procedural updates required to enforce the minimum coil cooling water flow. Maintenance approves the scope of inspections and updates to sensing and control elements. Final release contingent on completion of updates to SOP-P1-L3-05 and verification of control system configuration per ECN-2026-046 and SB-1026.
title: Change notice - Machining induction billet heater #1

text:
# ECN-2026-006 Change notice - Hot Forge induction billet heater #3

Revision: Rev B  
Plant: P3, line P3-L1  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L1-IH03

Reason for change
- Field inspection and failure mode analysis identified recurring coil overheating events tied to marginal coolant flow. To mitigate thermal stress and reduce unscheduled downtime, the minimum coil cooling water flow for Hot Forge induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P3-L1-IH03) is formally established as 65 L/min. This sets an operational threshold for monitoring and interlocks.

- Operator procedures and shift handover checklists for P3-L1.
- Maintenance and predictive monitoring routines that reference coil cooling criteria.

Implementation
- Update the control system alarm and interlock logic to enforce coil cooling water flow at or above 65 L/min. Configure a warning alarm for flow at the threshold and a gear-down or safe-stop interlock below the threshold per existing control architecture.
- Revise SOP-P3-L1-01 and SOP-P3-L1-03 to include the new minimum flow requirement and the required operator actions when flow approaches or falls below 65 L/min. Incorporate mandatory verification of flow readback during pre-start checks and transfer of care.
- Update maintenance scopes to include verification of flow meter calibration and valve actuation correlated to the specified minimum flow. Add coil cooling flow verification to the equipment preventive checklist referenced in ECN-2026-027.
- Execute implementation during the next scheduled planned outage window to avoid production disruption. Coordinate with operations and maintenance to validate alarm behavior and SOP revisions in a controlled startup.

- Operations concurrence recorded.  
- Maintenance approval obtained for revised preventive tasks.

# ECN-2026-022 - Change notice - Machining induction billet heater #1

Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P1, line P1-L3  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L3-IH01

Reason for change
- Recent operational checks and failure-mode analysis identified repeated trip events associated with low coil cooling flow on EQ-P1-L3-IH01. Root-cause investigation determined that the current control setpoints and alarm thresholds do not reflect the minimum required cooling to prevent coil overheating.
- To reduce unplanned downtime and mitigate accelerated insulation degradation, the coil cooling water flow minimum for Machining induction billet heater #1 (EQ-P1-L3-IH01) is 79 L/min. This value reflects the minimum safe hydraulic flow required to maintain coil thermal limits under standard machining duty.

Affected items
- Control system logic and alarm setpoint for coil cooling flow on EQ-P1-L3-IH01.
- Operator procedures for start-up, continuous monitoring, and response to low-flow alarms for the machining induction billet heater (see related SOPs).
- Preventive maintenance checklists that verify cooling circuit flow and filter condition prior to heater operation.

Implementation
- Update PLC analog input scaling and interlock logic to enforce the new minimum flow threshold and escalate alarms according to existing alarm hierarchy. Reference control change may require a ladder logic revision and tag update; coordinate with Controls group and document changes per ECN-2026-029.
- Revise SOP-P1-L3-01 and SOP-P1-L3-04 to incorporate the new minimum flow requirement, operator verification steps during start-up, and criteria for safe shutdown if flow cannot be achieved. Operators must confirm cooling flow meets or exceeds 79 L/min before enabling heater power.
- Update maintenance task sheets to include verification of flow metering accuracy and cooling circuit integrity prior to heater return to service. Capture completion of implementation tasks in the ECN record.

Approvals
- Implementation requires sign-off from Mechanical Maintenance, Controls Engineering, Operations Management, and Plant Reliability. Final ECN closure will be recorded in the document control system and cross-referenced to ECN-2026-029, SOP-P1-L3-01, and SOP-P1-L3-04.

Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P1, line P1-L1  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L1-RR01

## Reason for change
Operational feedback and bearing condition monitoring indicate accelerated grease depletion at the main roll bearing during standard production cycles. Analysis of lubricant consumption and bearing inspection records showed inconsistent grease distribution patterns originating from the current lubrication regimen. This change aligns the preventive maintenance practice with observed field conditions to reduce bearing wear, unplanned downtime, and potential scrap generation on the Hot Forge radial ring rolling mill #1.

Related documents: ECN-2026-034, ECN-2026-040, SOP-P1-L1-02

- Main roll bearing assembly on EQ-P1-L1-RR01
- Lubrication task list and maintenance instructions referenced in SOP-P1-L1-02

## Implementation
Update the maintenance procedure for EQ-P1-L1-RR01 to set the main roll bearing lubrication interval for Hot Forge radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P1-L1-RR01) to 120 hours. Technicians shall follow the lubrication method and approved lubricant specified in SOP-P1-L1-02 when performing the task. Replace the current task entry in the computerized maintenance system with the revised interval and ensure that the maintenance checklist for EQ-P1-L1-RR01 reflects the new interval. Conduct a focused training briefing for maintenance personnel on the updated interval and verification steps prior to the next scheduled maintenance window. Inspect and document grease distribution at the time of the first lubrication action under the new interval and enter findings in the maintenance log.

## Approvals

Plant: P3, line P3-L1

Reason for change
- During recent inspections, cooling circuit performance for EQ-P3-L1-IH03 was observed to be degraded under certain load conditions. To prevent thermal degradation of the induction coil and associated insulation, the minimum acceptable coil cooling water flow rate has been formalized.
- The coil cooling water flow minimum for Hot Forge induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P3-L1-IH03) is 65 L/min. This threshold defines the lower operational limit below which heater operation shall be restricted and corrective action initiated.

Affected items
- EQ-P3-L1-IH03 control logic and HMI alarm setpoints that reference cooling water flow.
- Preventive maintenance check sheets and test procedures that verify cooling water flow for EQ-P3-L1-IH03.
- Operator runbooks and startup/shutdown checklists that govern safe operation of EQ-P3-L1-IH03.

Implementation
- Update the PLC alarm configuration for EQ-P3-L1-IH03 to reflect the new minimum flow threshold and ensure HMI displays the condition prominently.
- Revise the preventive maintenance checklist for EQ-P3-L1-IH03 to require verification of cooling water flow against the stated minimum. Use SOP-P3-L1-02, SOP-P3-L1-03, and SOP-P3-L1-05 for procedure alignment and to update steps referencing cooling circuit checks.
- Train operations and maintenance personnel on the new minimum flow requirement and the required response if flow falls below 65 L/min. Training records shall be retained per plant document control practice and referenced in the equipment file.
- Implement immediate manual verification after change deployment and schedule follow-up verification per the maintenance program.

- Engineering Lead: (signature on file)
- Maintenance Manager: (signature on file)

- Field verification and audit of process records identified inconsistent quench timing for EQ-P2-L2-HT02 during ring rolling heat treat cycles. - Operator instructions and checklists used on P2-L2 line.

- The quench delay maximum for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L2-HT02) is 16 seconds.

# ECN-2026-031 Change notice - Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #2

Reason for change
- Update required to clarify and enforce quench sequencing for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L2-HT02). Field validation identified inconsistent quench timing reporting during production runs on P2, line P2-L2. To eliminate variability in mechanical properties of rolled rings, the documented maximum quench delay for EQ-P2-L2-HT02 is defined and mandated.

Affected items
- Process control specification and operator checklists for EQ-P2-L2-HT02 used on P2, line P2-L2.
- Shop travelers and heat treat route sheets referencing furnace behavior for ring rolling parts.
- Training materials and shift handover logs that govern quench initiation procedures.
- Quality inspection hold points tied to heat treat cycle monitoring.

Implementation
- The quench delay maximum for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L2-HT02) is 16 seconds. This value shall be entered into the furnace PLC alarm setpoints and the heat treat data acquisition system without modification.
- Update MM-P2-L2-HT02 to reflect the enforced quench delay maximum and include a step to verify alarm setpoint presence before production start.
- Revise operator procedure in QS-PROC-08 to require confirmation of the 16 seconds quench delay maximum during shift pre-start checks and to document any deviation as a stop-work condition pending maintenance action.
- Engineering to deploy a software update to the furnace HMI and data logger to record quench initiation timestamps and generate alerts when the quench delay exceeds the specified maximum. Reference ECN-2026-028 for the baseline change logic to be incorporated.
- Production shall not resume on P2, line P2-L2 for runs requiring EQ-P2-L2-HT02 until implementation steps are complete and verified.

Approvals
- Requested approvals required from Heat Treat Engineering, Quality Assurance, and Plant Operations. See ECN-2026-028, MM-P2-L2-HT02, QS-PROC-08 for related procedures and prior authorizations to facilitate review and closure.

Reason for change
- Field verification during setup identified that tooling limits and the control system parameter did not reflect the final customer requirement for larger parts. - Operator and maintenance procedures that reference ring size limits: SOP-P2-L2-05.
- Preventive maintenance and inspection checklists referenced in MM-P2-L2-RR03.

- Revise MM-P2-L2-RR03 maintenance entries to include visual verification of nameplate and parameter integrity after configuration change, and to reference SB-1017 for any safety-related modifications.
- Post updated notices at the machine and within the control room. Circulate revised procedure copies and provide a one-time training brief to operators and maintenance personnel covering the change and the implications for setup and inspection.

Approvals
- Engineering change approved by Plant Engineering and Operations leadership. Required references: MM-P2-L2-RR03, SB-1017, SOP-P2-L2-05.
